ON Could Be One of the Semiconductor Sector’s Biggest Comeback Stories
ON Semiconductor crashed hard in 2025, but the numbers coming out of its latest quarter tell a very different story, and the question now is whether the market has fully caught on yet.
Published October 13, 2026, 1:30pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
The glowing core of a microchip symbolizes the immense processing power and surging AI demand currently fueling record revenues for semiconductor giants like AMD and Nvidia. © 24/7 Wall St.
The 24/7 Wall St. price target for ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) is $96.51 over the next 12 months. From a recent price of $77.53, that works out to 24.48% upside. The stock gets a buy rating from our model, and its confidence is high.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
ON has climbed out of the trough. Revenue fell 22.39% year over year in Q1 2025, then grew 9.18% in Q2 2026. Management now expects AI data center revenue to more than double in 2026, and Q3 guidance calls for non-GAAP EPS of $0.81-$0.93.
A 42% Rally Interrupted by a Sharp Pullback
The stock is up 42.27% year to date and 54.17% over the past year. Over the past week it fell 9.25%, though it is still up 8.54% over the past month. Shares sit well below the 52-week high of $134.92 and well above the low of $44.56.
In Q2, revenue came in at $1.6035B, beating estimates by 0.89%. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.74 against a $0.7153 estimate. Free cash flow reached $425.4M. ON also put through a price adjustment that took effect on October 10, which points to firm demand.
Management raised its 2030 AI data center addressable market from $12 billion to almost $50 billion. All of that expansion still has to be powered, cooled, and connected by somebody, and we rounded up seven of those suppliers in a free AI infrastructure report. Lead times extended from approximately 27 weeks to approximately 32 weeks.
Utilization rose to 83%, and each additional point adds 25 to 30 basis points of gross margin. A $6B buyback adds further support. Among analysts, 2 rate the stock a strong buy and 12 rate it a buy. Our bull case reaches $120.73.
Barclays started coverage at equal-weight with a $75 target and noted ON’s automotive and China exposure. Analog and Mixed-Signal revenue fell 2%. The Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) deal, expected to close in mid-2027, brings integration risk, and the convertible notes could dilute shareholders.
The trailing P/E of 249 looks alarming, but it reflects low 2025 earnings, including $666.9M of restructuring charges. Those charges dropped to $41.2M in Q2. The bear case sits at $79.59.
ON Trades Between NXP and Texas Instruments
NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) is ON’s most direct automotive and industrial rival. It trades at 13x forward earnings while growing revenue 19.48%, so ON looks pricier on recovery-stage earnings.
Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN) is the analog and power benchmark. It commands 28x forward earnings on 22.82% growth. Our target implies about 24x forward EPS, which sits between the two. That looks reasonable as long as ON’s margins keep recovering.
ON Semiconductor Price Prediction 2026-2030
I see the 24/7 Wall St. price target of $96.51 as well supported, and our model’s buy rating carries 90% confidence. Operating leverage is the key factor.
The thesis gets stronger if Q3 gross margin lands within the 40%-42% guidance. It weakens if automotive demand fades or the Synaptics integration struggles. I think the recovery has further to run.
Going forward, here is where our model projects ON could trade, assuming current growth trends and market conditions hold.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
These projections assume ON keeps executing its current strategy. The adoption of 800-volt data center architectures could push results higher, while a decline in automotive demand could pull them lower.

Jim Cramer on semiconductor stocks after six-day sell off
CNBC’s Jim Cramer said investors shouldn't give up on semiconductor stocks despite the recent sell-off, arguing that strong demand for chips continues to support the industry's long-term growth.
Cramer highlighted Micron's long-term customer agreements and the expanding use of CPUs from Intel and AMD as reasons the sector's underlying fundamentals remain strong.
The memory group has been the most beaten up and discouraging, says Jim Cramer
Semiconductor stocks have been getting crushed in recent days, but CNBC's Jim Cramer said Tuesday there's a compelling reason not to give up on the group.
The VanEck Semiconductor ETF has fallen 7.2% over six consecutive sessions, and Cramer warned that rising oil prices and interest rates could prolong the sell off. However, he argued chip stocks are increasingly trading together regardless of their individual fundamentals, obscuring the strong demand that fueled the sector's remarkable rally earlier this year.
To illustrate his point, Cramer described a recent visit to an Apple showroom, where he saw devices featuring a more personalized Siri and advanced smart home technology. The experience highlighted how increasingly sophisticated consumer products require more computing power and memory, creating additional opportunities for chipmakers.
"Before you decide to bail from the semis because you can't take the pain, go to the showroom," the "Mad Money" host said. "Go see where these chips are used. They appear in places that you'd least expect them. Don't watch the semiconductor index, watch the devices."
Cramer pointed to memory chip maker Micron as an example of a company whose fundamentals are being overshadowed by the broader sell off. The company has become one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence build-out, with demand for memory chips far outstripping supply. Cramer highlighted its 26 long-term customer agreements, which currently cover about 35% of revenue through 2030, with negotiations already underway for 2031. Those take-or-pay contracts require customers to honor their financial commitments, he said, giving Micron greater visibility into future revenue. "If Micron had no agreements I would be worried," Cramer said.
And the demand story isn't limited to memory chips. Cramer also highlighted Intel and AMD, which "make the CPUs that are basic building blocks for practically every machine under the sun."
Cramer acknowledged that the group could face further losses after its enormous run, but said investors shouldn't dismiss the fundamental demand behind those gains. "It's reasonable to expect a sharp pullback after how far these stocks traveled," he said. "I just think that when you see the devices, when you know the exploding use cases, you can understand why Micron or Intel or AMD have been moving up."
"It wasn't all Situational Awareness, the wayward hedge fund that took so many semis up to unsustainable levels with borrowed money," Cramer said. "A lot of this is just raw demand."
Cramer's Charitable Trust, the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club, owns shares of AAPL, INTC, MU.

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.
Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.
We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

On Semiconductor Climbs 8%, Synaptics Surges 14% as $5.7B Cash Bid Replaces $7B Stock Deal
On Semiconductor scrapped its stock deal for Synaptics and replaced it with cash, and both stocks surged on the news for reasons that point in opposite directions.
Published October 2, 2026, 9:13am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.
Under an amended merger agreement, On Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, replacing the all-stock structure. The amendment followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party.
On Semiconductor now expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share upon closing. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
Synaptics also brings growth. Its management expects fiscal 2026 Core Internet of Things (IoT) revenue to grow more than 40% to over $385 million, driven by Edge AI and Physical AI design wins. On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”
The trade-off is debt. Cash and short-term investments totaled $3.9 billion at the end of Q2, with total liquidity of $5.4 billion. Quarterly free cash flow reached $425 million, a support for paying down new borrowing.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.
Investors can watch for the Synaptics stockholder vote and remaining reviews in other jurisdictions before On Semiconductor closes the purchase, as details on the committed debt financing cost could shape how the market judges On Semiconductor’s balance sheet.
Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.
Synaptics shareholders now face an outcome fixed at the $123 cash price. Traders may watch whether On Semiconductor stock holds its gains as borrowing terms become clearer.

ON Semiconductor (ISIN US6821891035) raised its long-term revenue growth target to 12% to 14% annually through 2030 from 10% to 12%. Druckfin reported on September 16, 2026 that management also modeled revenue of USD 11.00 billion by 2030 and retained a 53.00 percent gross-margin target. The larger ambition puts execution and margin delivery at the center of the stock story.
ON Semiconductor's second-quarter 2026 revenue was USD 1.60 billion, up 9.20 percent year over year, while adjusted earnings per share reached USD 0.74 against a USD 0.72 consensus estimate. MarketBeat said on September 29, 2026 that revenue exceeded the USD 1.59 billion forecast and that third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share guidance was USD 0.81 to USD 0.93.
The comparison is important because the growth target is forward-looking, while the latest reported quarter already delivered a 9.20 percent revenue increase. Management's third-quarter guidance therefore gives investors a nearer-term test of whether higher factory utilization can translate into stronger profitability.
Stifel lowered its price target for ON Semiconductor from USD 90.00 to USD 75.00 and kept a Hold rating after the September 16, 2026 analyst day. Investing.com reported that the firm viewed the 12% to 14% revenue compound annual growth target, 53.00 percent gross margin target and 38.00 percent operating-margin target as potentially below expectations.
The split between a higher corporate growth ambition and a lower analyst target creates a clear valuation tension. The market must ultimately judge whether the planned growth rate can produce the margin expansion embedded in the 2030 framework.
ON Semiconductor had a market capitalization of USD 29.9 billion as of September 30, 2026. Its 52-week range was USD 44.56 to USD 134.92, placing the latest primary-market quote of USD 76.87 materially below the yearly high while keeping the stock above its yearly low.

onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:01 AM CDT 5 min read
Advanced EliteSiC hybrid technology maximizes usable energy as electricity demand surges
As AI-driven electricity demand accelerates worldwide, utilities and energy providers are under growing pressure to store and deliver energy more efficiently. Battery energy storage system (BESS) providers are seeking advanced power conversion technologies to improve performance and system economics. To address these needs, Sungrow has adopted onsemi's latest SiC hybrid power module technology for its PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The design improves system efficiency, helping utilities and energy providers increase usable energy output while lowering operating costs.
onsemi's EliteSiC hybrid power module enables the highest-density battery energy storage system deployments, helping energy providers meet growing electricity demand from AI, renewable energy and electrification
New BESS architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, helping maximize energy delivered to the grid while reducing losses and improving reliability
Sungrow's PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform integrates onsemi's latest EliteSiC hybrid power module technology, optimized for high-power DC-AC energy conversion in utility-scale battery storage applications
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) today announced that Sungrow, a global leader in renewable energy technology, has adopted onsemi's latest EliteSiC silicon carbide (SiC) hybrid power module technology for the Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The integration enables improved efficiency and enhanced system performance for utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Helping Sungrow Deliver More Usable Energy
The PowerTitan 3.0 platform incorporates onsemi's high-density power integrated modules (PIMs), optimized for advanced three-level inverter architectures used in high-power energy storage applications.
Compared with the previous-generation platform, the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, enabling higher-power battery storage deployments without sacrificing efficiency. The architecture supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW, contributing to the platform's increased power density and higher-power deployment capability.
With the performance advantages of SiC, the solution supports key system-level benefits including:
Peak efficiency exceeding 99.3% to reduce energy loss in utility-scale systems
Increased power density supports higher-power BESS deployments
Enhanced thermal performance supports reliable operation in high-power applications
Improved system economics through a hybrid SiC design optimized for large-scale deployment
The design win builds on a long-standing strategic relationship between onsemi and Sungrow. Through extensive engineering and validation activities, the companies collaborated throughout platform definition, system optimization and qualification to meet the demanding performance requirements of next-generation energy storage deployments.
"PowerTitan 3.0 represents Sungrow's continued innovation in advanced energy storage system design," said Chen Peng, General Manager of Energy Storage Conversion Product Line at Sungrow Energy Storage Business Unit. "By integrating advanced technologies and collaborating with strategic partners such as onsemi, Sungrow is accelerating the deployment of higher-performance storage solutions that deliver greater value throughout the lifecycle of energy assets. With growing market recognition, Sungrow estimates delivering 10 GWh of PowerTitan 3.0 across Europe in 2026, further supporting the region's transition toward a more flexible and resilient energy system."
"At utility scale, even small improvements in power conversion efficiency can have a meaningful impact on battery energy storage system (BESS) performance and total cost of ownership," said Sergio Fissore, Vice President and General Manager, IPD Power Division, onsemi. "Our EliteSiC hybrid power module enables higher-efficiency, higher-density energy storage systems that help maximize usable energy and improve system reliability. Together with Sungrow, we're advancing the power conversion technologies needed to support the next generation of energy infrastructure."
At utility scale, even small efficiency improvements can generate meaningful financial and environmental benefits. According to onsemi analysis, a 0.4% efficiency improvement delivered by the new SiC hybrid module could save more than 475 MWh of energy annually in a 100 MW battery energy storage installation compared with the previous-generation module.
Those energy savings can help reduce operating costs, increase usable energy delivered to customers and lower overall emissions. The architecture also enables higher overload capability and improved thermal performance, helping customers extract more usable energy from every storage asset.
Supporting the Infrastructure Behind the AI Era
Utilities and energy providers are seeking ways to store more energy, reduce conversion losses and improve overall system economics to meet unprecedented demand amid the AI infrastructure buildout and electrification transition.
Industry forecasts project the battery energy storage market will more than double by 2030 as utilities invest in infrastructure needed to support increasing electricity demand and renewable energy deployment. At the same time, energy storage providers are moving toward higher-power, higher-voltage architectures to improve system economics.

onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
Revised Terms to Deliver Higher onsemi Shareholder Value through Immediate EPS Accretion
Amended Agreement Follows Thorough Review of Unsolicited Competing Proposal
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif. – Oct. 1, 2026 – onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended
their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7
billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger
agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration,
and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate
synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months
post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s
evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the
combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the
best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel,
Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley.
The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary
closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.
More Information:
Investor Presentation: onsemi & Synaptics Revised Merger Terms1
onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) delivers intelligent power and sensing technologies that enable electrification, energy efficiency, safety, and automation across automotive,
industrial, and AI data center end‑markets. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi helps customers solve complex challenges to achieve higher efficiency, improved performance, and lower system cost, while supporting a
safer, cleaner, and more energy‑efficient world. The company is part of the S&P 500® index. Learn more at www.onsemi.com.
Synaptics (Nasdaq: SYNA) is driving innovation in AI at the Edge, bringing AI closer to end users and transforming how we engage with intelligent connected devices,
whether at home, at work, or on the move. As a go-to partner for forward-thinking product innovators, Synaptics powers the future with its cutting-edge Synaptics Astra™ AI-Native embedded compute, wireless connectivity, and multimodal sensing
solutions. We’re making the digital experience smarter, faster, more intuitive, secure, and seamless. From touch, display, and biometrics to AI-driven wireless connectivity, video, vision, audio, speech, and security processing, Synaptics is a
force behind the next generation of technology enhancing how we live, work, and play.
Vice President - Investor Relations & Corporate Development

the SEC a preliminary proxy statement on Schedule 14A. Promptly after filing its definitive proxy statement with the SEC, Synaptics will send the definitive proxy statement to each stockholder entitled to vote at the special meeting relating to the
transaction. Synaptics also plans to file other documents with the SEC regarding the proposed transaction. This document is not a substitute for the proxy statement or any other document which Synaptics may file with the SEC in connection with the

obtain free copies of the definitive proxy statement, preliminary proxy statement and other documents filed with the SEC by Synaptics on the Synaptics Investor Relations website at https://investor.synaptics.com/.

participants in the solicitation of proxies from Synaptics stockholders in connection with the proposed transaction. Information regarding the persons who may, under the rules of the SEC, be deemed participants in the solicitation of Synaptics

April 2, 2026. To the extent holdings of onsemi common stock by the directors and executive officers of onsemi have changed from the amounts of onsemi common stock held by such persons as reflected therein, such changes have been or will be

Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT) and CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD) each reported roughly 26% revenue growth in their latest quarters. Investors nevertheless pay about 53 times Fortinet’s current-year adjusted earnings guidance and 215 times CrowdStrike’s. The gap raises a useful question: how much more should durable subscription growth cost when the cheaper company already earns substantial reported profits?
The multiples use October 2 closing prices of $180.95 and $270.04, divided by guidance midpoints of $3.44 and $1.255. Fortinet’s year ends December 2026; CrowdStrike’s ends January 2027. CrowdStrike’s price and earnings are both adjusted for July’s four-for-one split. Our earlier CrowdStrike–Palo Alto valuation comparison tests a different rival; Fortinet adds a sharper hardware-versus-subscription challenge.
The same growth rate hides different engines
Fortinet’s June-quarter product revenue jumped 52%, while services grew 14%. Hardware demand can arrive in bursts as customers upgrade networks.Converting the product surge into recurring service revenue would make growth more durable when the hardware upgrade cycle slows. That matters when judging the businesses in our high-growth, low-debt stock screen: financial flexibility and growth durability answer different questions.
CrowdStrike’s July-quarter ending annual recurring revenue grew 25% to $5.84 billion. Net new ARR increased 51% to $333 million, supporting a case for accelerating customer commitments. Its security platform spans endpoints, identity and cloud workloads. Our agentic-AI stock shortlist examines where security fits among the platforms companies need as automated work spreads.
Fortinet is also expanding beyond appliances. Management reported 35% billings growth in Unified SASE, which combines networking and security services, and 25% in AI-driven Security Operations. These are billings measures, not recognized revenue. The premium requires more durable, profitable growth. Our analysis of cybersecurity’s split from the AI infrastructure trade asks why security budgets might follow a different spending cycle.
Insider Monkey’s Q2 2026 holder count rose to 62 from 52 in Q1 for Fortinet and to 89 from 79 for CrowdStrike. Arrowstreet increased Fortinet shares about 5%; D. E. Shaw increased CrowdStrike shares 18%. The competing business models both drew broader fund ownership.
Reported profits change the burden of proof
Fortinet earned a 33.7% GAAP operating margin in Q2. CrowdStrike recorded a $33.2 million GAAP operating loss on $1.47 billion of revenue, despite substantial adjusted profit. CrowdStrike’s reconciliation adds back $399 million of stock compensation and related payroll taxes, about 27% of revenue. That makes a fourfold adjusted-earnings multiple gap especially demanding.
Cash flow provides a second lens. Fortinet generated reported $966 million of free cash flow, or 47.2% of revenue, while CrowdStrike reported $377 million, or about 26%; their free-cash-flow definitions differ. Collections and working capital make one quarter an imperfect comparison, and stock compensation can support cash flow while diluting shareholders. Our cash-flow screen that includes Fortinet examines that distinction; our return-on-equity ranking shows why high reported profitability also needs a balance-sheet check.
CrowdStrike’s strongest defense is a longer growth runway. Security agents could increase the value of its installed platform and proprietary customer context. The commercial question behind its cybersecurity work with Nvidia is whether that advantage becomes incremental revenue. Its expanded OpenAI partnership presents a related test: better models must strengthen pricing power enough to offset competition and deployment costs.
How much execution does the premium require?
As an illustration, if Fortinet’s adjusted earnings per share grew 15% annually for five years with both share prices unchanged, CrowdStrike would need roughly 52% annual earnings-per-share growth to reach Fortinet’s resulting multiple of about 26 times earnings. This is a valuation sensitivity, not a forecast; faster Fortinet growth would raise the hurdle. CrowdStrike can outperform without fully closing the gap, but continued premium pricing carries risk.
CrowdStrike’s September 15 short interest was 27.93 million shares, approximately 2.8% of float, with 2.42 days to cover. That dated snapshot offers limited support for a squeeze thesis.
Fortinet is my relative preference, though 53 times guided earnings still requires sustained growth. I would reconsider if its service growth stalls while CrowdStrike converts rising ARR into much faster per-share profits with less dilution. The risk explored in our analysis of AI and cybersecurity moats matters to both: stronger tools can expand demand while narrowing product differences. CrowdStrike must monetize that change exceptionally well to justify today’s price.

A suspected state-sponsored threat actor exploited multiple Fortinet vulnerabilities in an attack against a telecommunications organization, Palo Alto Networks reports.
The intrusion, attributed to UNC5820 (tracked by Palo Alto Networks as CL-STA-0954), occurred in September 2024 and resulted in long-term access to the victim’s environment.
Initial access was obtained through the exploitation of a critical remote code execution (RCE) bug in FortiManager, tracked as CVE-2024-47575 and patched in October 2024 as a zero-day.
Shortly after the patches were rolled out, Mandiant warned that UNC5820 had been exploiting the flaw, named FortiJump, since at least June 2024.
A fresh report from Palo Alto Networks shows that UNC5820 also exploited CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal vulnerability affecting multiple Fortinet products, as part of the same intrusion.
Impacting FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager and patched in April 2026, the security defect could allow authenticated attackers to write or delete arbitrary files. Fortinet flagged its exploitation as a zero-day at the time of disclosure.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
On Friday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2025-61624 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, urging federal agencies to patch it immediately.
UNC5820 appears to have exploited the path traversal as a zero-day to deploy a previously unknown FortiGate implant dubbed PeerStitch.
The ARM64 malware resides in memory, avoids opening listening ports or initiating outbound network connections, and communicates through the traffic generated by legitimate processes on the appliance.
As part of the observed attack, UNC5820 exploited FortiJump to access a central FortiManager instance, registered a rogue Virtual FortiGate appliance, and exfiltrated a configuration archive containing details on FortiManager, more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and the victim’s network.
UNC5820 exploited CVE-2025-61624 to gain root access to the underlying firewall operating system, dropping a script to initiate the PeerStitch deployment.
Written in C, the implant acts as a ‘one-shot process memory patching injector’ targeting the central system and traffic logging, and the IKE/IPsec VPN service daemons in FortiOS to create a covert, memory-resident communication bridge between them and bypass default FortiOS security validations.
As part of the attack, the threat actor was also seen impersonating FortiManager in FortiGate-to-FortiManager (FGFM) communications to issue commands from external infrastructure and “took extensive measures to eliminate forensic artifacts”.
According to Palo Alto Networks, UNC5820 asserted the management identity either by terminating the authentic FortiManager’s session by exploiting CVE-2024-26008, or by reusing exfiltrated secrets and authenticating as the legitimate FortiManager.
“The discovery of the PeerStitch implant demonstrates the increasing technical maturity of edge-device malware. By operating as a one-shot injector, avoiding persistent disk artifacts and building a covert inter-process communication bridge inside process memory, the attackers achieved sustained persistence while evading traditional monitoring,” Palo Alto Networks notes.

Can Fortinet's SASE Momentum Propel the Stock to New Highs?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 7:47 AM CDT 3 min read
Fortinet FTNT is gaining traction with its push to converge firewall and secure access service edge (SASE) technologies, positioning the stock for upside. At its SASE Summit 2026, highlighted on Oct. 8, the company outlined how its Unified SASE platform is evolving to secure AI applications and autonomous agents alongside human users.
Fortinet is addressing sovereignty demands through FortiSASE Outpost, which extends inspection and enforcement to on-premises and colocation sites under centralized cloud management, and FortiSASE Sovereign, a private SASE model that customers or service providers can run on their infrastructure.
This builds on the FortiGate 1200G series launched with FortiSASE Outpost in July, which combines ASIC-powered local enforcement with cloud-delivered security. The strategy is showing up in results. In second-quarter 2026, the combined SASE Firewall business, spanning Secure Networking and Unified SASE, grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings rose 35%, while FortiSASE billings more than doubled. Billings jumped 33% year over year to $2.37 billion, and revenues climbed 26% to $2.05 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Fundamentals reinforce the outlook. Product revenues surged 52% to $773 million, with management expecting attached services to boost service revenue growth in the second half. Meanwhile, the non-GAAP operating margin hit a second-quarter record of 38%.
Backed by this momentum, Fortinet raised its 2026 outlook and now expects revenues of $8.02-$8.18 billion, implying 19% growth, billings of $9.35-$9.55 billion and service revenues of $5.18-$5.22 billion. Non-GAAP operating margin is projected at 35-37%, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.41-$3.47. For the third quarter, it expects revenues of $2.01-$2.10 billion, billings of $2.25-$2.35 billion and non-GAAP EPS of 83-87 cents.
With SASE emerging as a growth engine and guidance pointing to sustained billings strength, Fortinet appears well placed to extend its momentum, paving the way for the stock to reach new highs.
How Fortinet Stacks Up Against PANW and ZS in SASE
Fortinet faces competition in SASE from Palo Alto Networks PANW and Zscaler ZS. Palo Alto Networks' Next-Generation Security ARR, which includes SASE, grew 63% to $9.10 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter 2026, while SASE competitive displacements totaled about $450 million for the fiscal year.
Palo Alto Networks expects fiscal 2027 NGS ARR of $11.08-$11.18 billion. Zscaler, a cloud-native zero-trust provider, grew ARR 25% to $3.77 billion in the same quarter and ended with more than 950 Zero Trust Everywhere enterprises. Zscaler projects fiscal 2027 ARR of $4.40-$4.43 billion. Unlike Zscaler's cloud-delivered approach, Fortinet offers on-premises, hybrid and sovereign SASE deployments.
FTNT's Share Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Fortinet shares have gained 116% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Security industry and the broader Computer and Technology sector's growth of 81.8% and 15.8%, respectively.
From a valuation standpoint, FTNT appears overvalued, trading at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings ratio of 45.52, higher than the sector's average of 19.44. The company carries a Value Score of F.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Fortinet's earnings is pegged at $3.45 per share for 2026, which implies year-over-year growth of 25%.

Investors seek growth stocks to capitalize on above-average growth in financials that help these securities grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. However, it isn't easy to find a great growth stock.

NET vs. FTNT: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:42 AM CDT 5 min read
Cloudflare NET and Fortinet Inc. FTNT are well-known players in the cybersecurity domain. While Cloudflare provides a cloud-native platform spanning network security, application security and connectivity, Fortinet combines a variety of hardware and cloud-based security solutions.
Both NET and FTNT are riding key industry trends, driven by the mounting incidents of credential theft, remote desktop protocol breaches and social engineering-based strikes by malicious actors. However, from an investment perspective, one stock offers a more favorable outlook than the other right now. Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which stock offers a more compelling investment case.
Cloudflare is seeing stronger demand for its SASE and Zero Trust offerings as companies look to adopt AI more securely. Management said the key reason big companies are approaching Cloudflare is that they know they need AI but want to deploy it securely. This is creating new opportunities for the company's SASE and Zero Trust platforms, particularly as enterprises need to secure AI agents in addition to human users.
Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach gives it an advantage in this market. Management said companies will have more AI agents working across their organizations and will need a security model designed for these agents. In one example, a large U.K. government agency was evaluating a first-generation Zero Trust provider but reconsidered the project after discussing its plans for AI agents with Cloudflare. Management said the agency canceled its existing request for proposal and is now reevaluating the project with an agents-first approach. Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach has helped its SASE and Zero Trust platforms gain significant share over the past six months.
However, Cloudflare's non-GAAP gross margin was 73.1% in the second quarter of 2026, down 320 basis points from 76.3% a year ago. The main issue is the changing mix of traffic on Cloudflare's network. As paid traffic grows relative to free traffic, a larger portion of Cloudflare's network costs is being allocated to cost of revenue. This shows that Cloudflare is handling more traffic that requires infrastructure and network resources, putting pressure on gross margins.
This is particularly relevant as AI workloads and machine-to-machine traffic expand. These workloads can drive more usage and revenues, but they also require Cloudflare to provide more compute, network and storage capacity. Although management expects gross-margin pressure to stabilize, continued growth in AI and developer workloads could require higher infrastructure spending. This could limit near-term margin expansion even as revenues continue to grow rapidly.
Fortinet is seeing strong demand for its SASE Firewall as enterprises upgrade network security to support AI workloads, cloud environments and distributed workforces. In the second quarter of 2026, Fortinet's SASE Firewall business grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings increased 35%, while FortiSASE billings grew more than 100% year over year. FortiSASE adoption also reached 90% of Fortinet's large-enterprise installed base.
Fortinet believes its SASE Firewall can address a larger market than cloud-only SASE solutions. The company combines firewall, SASE and hybrid mesh capabilities on its FortiOS platform and supports both cloud and on-premises deployments. Management believes this opportunity could be two to three times larger than the cloud-only SASE market. Demand for sovereign SASE is also increasing as enterprises and service providers look for better data privacy, local processing and performance.
AI is adding another growth driver. As AI applications increase machine-to-machine and data-center traffic, customers need better visibility and control over network traffic. Fortinet said AI is accelerating the convergence of networking and security. The company is also seeing AI data center wins, including an eight-figure deal with a cloud provider offering generative AI infrastructure.
The growth in SASE could also support Fortinet's financial performance. Product revenues increased 52% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while service revenues grew 14% year over year. Service billings increased 26% year over year, and management expects service revenue growth to improve in the second half of 2026. New SASE and SD-WAN services can add to Fortinet's recurring service revenues as customers expand their deployments. With strong SASE demand, AI-driven security needs and growing adoption of sovereign SASE, the SASE Firewall could become an important driver of Fortinet's product and service revenue growth.

Conclusion: Buy FTNT, Sell NET Right Now

Fortinet, Inc. (NASDAQ:FTNT) and CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD) each reported roughly 26% revenue growth in their latest quarters. Investors nevertheless pay about 53 times Fortinet’s current-year adjusted earnings guidance and 215 times CrowdStrike’s. The gap raises a useful question: how much more should durable subscription growth cost when the cheaper company already earns substantial reported profits?
The multiples use October 2 closing prices of $180.95 and $270.04, divided by guidance midpoints of $3.44 and $1.255. Fortinet’s year ends December 2026; CrowdStrike’s ends January 2027. CrowdStrike’s price and earnings are both adjusted for July’s four-for-one split. Our earlier CrowdStrike–Palo Alto valuation comparison tests a different rival; Fortinet adds a sharper hardware-versus-subscription challenge.
The same growth rate hides different engines
Fortinet’s June-quarter product revenue jumped 52%, while services grew 14%. Hardware demand can arrive in bursts as customers upgrade networks.Converting the product surge into recurring service revenue would make growth more durable when the hardware upgrade cycle slows. That matters when judging the businesses in our high-growth, low-debt stock screen: financial flexibility and growth durability answer different questions.
CrowdStrike’s July-quarter ending annual recurring revenue grew 25% to $5.84 billion. Net new ARR increased 51% to $333 million, supporting a case for accelerating customer commitments. Its security platform spans endpoints, identity and cloud workloads. Our agentic-AI stock shortlist examines where security fits among the platforms companies need as automated work spreads.
Fortinet is also expanding beyond appliances. Management reported 35% billings growth in Unified SASE, which combines networking and security services, and 25% in AI-driven Security Operations. These are billings measures, not recognized revenue. The premium requires more durable, profitable growth. Our analysis of cybersecurity’s split from the AI infrastructure trade asks why security budgets might follow a different spending cycle.
Insider Monkey’s Q2 2026 holder count rose to 62 from 52 in Q1 for Fortinet and to 89 from 79 for CrowdStrike. Arrowstreet increased Fortinet shares about 5%; D. E. Shaw increased CrowdStrike shares 18%. The competing business models both drew broader fund ownership.
Reported profits change the burden of proof
Fortinet earned a 33.7% GAAP operating margin in Q2. CrowdStrike recorded a $33.2 million GAAP operating loss on $1.47 billion of revenue, despite substantial adjusted profit. CrowdStrike’s reconciliation adds back $399 million of stock compensation and related payroll taxes, about 27% of revenue. That makes a fourfold adjusted-earnings multiple gap especially demanding.
Cash flow provides a second lens. Fortinet generated reported $966 million of free cash flow, or 47.2% of revenue, while CrowdStrike reported $377 million, or about 26%; their free-cash-flow definitions differ. Collections and working capital make one quarter an imperfect comparison, and stock compensation can support cash flow while diluting shareholders. Our cash-flow screen that includes Fortinet examines that distinction; our return-on-equity ranking shows why high reported profitability also needs a balance-sheet check.
CrowdStrike’s strongest defense is a longer growth runway. Security agents could increase the value of its installed platform and proprietary customer context. The commercial question behind its cybersecurity work with Nvidia is whether that advantage becomes incremental revenue. Its expanded OpenAI partnership presents a related test: better models must strengthen pricing power enough to offset competition and deployment costs.
How much execution does the premium require?
As an illustration, if Fortinet’s adjusted earnings per share grew 15% annually for five years with both share prices unchanged, CrowdStrike would need roughly 52% annual earnings-per-share growth to reach Fortinet’s resulting multiple of about 26 times earnings. This is a valuation sensitivity, not a forecast; faster Fortinet growth would raise the hurdle. CrowdStrike can outperform without fully closing the gap, but continued premium pricing carries risk.
CrowdStrike’s September 15 short interest was 27.93 million shares, approximately 2.8% of float, with 2.42 days to cover. That dated snapshot offers limited support for a squeeze thesis.
Fortinet is my relative preference, though 53 times guided earnings still requires sustained growth. I would reconsider if its service growth stalls while CrowdStrike converts rising ARR into much faster per-share profits with less dilution. The risk explored in our analysis of AI and cybersecurity moats matters to both: stronger tools can expand demand while narrowing product differences. CrowdStrike must monetize that change exceptionally well to justify today’s price.

CBTS and Fortinet Launch Fully Managed Secure Networking Service for Growing Mid-Market Organizations
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 5 min read
New CBTS service brings networking and security into one platform, managed 24x7 for organizations with lean IT teams
CBTS brings firewalls, switching, wireless, and SD-WAN onto a single Fortinet platform that CBTS designs, deploys, and operates.
The service is built for mid-market and multi-site organizations that need stronger networking and security capabilities, without adding specialized in-house staff.
CBTS brings Fortinet-certified engineers, proven reference architectures, and 24x7 operations under one accountable team and one monthly subscription.
CINCINNATI, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--CBTS, a leading North American technology services company, today launched CBTS Fortinet Managed Services. The new fully managed secure networking service helps mid-market and multi-site organizations modernize aging infrastructure, strengthen security, and support growth without adding network and security headcount.
Mid-market organizations are caught between the sophistication of today's threats and the resources available to defend against a growing attack surface. According to Forrester Research, security and risk leaders entering the 2027 planning cycle face persistent challenges, including platform sprawl, talent scarcity, rising costs, and growing pressure from AI-enabled threats. As adversaries gain access to more advanced AI capabilities, already-stretched security teams will face greater pressure to detect and respond to threats quickly.1
Chris DeBrunner, CISO at CBTS, said: "For most mid-market organizations, hiring their way out of the problem is no longer realistic. CBTS gives them another option: bring networking and security together on a single platform, operated by certified CBTS engineers 24 hours a day."
One platform, one partner, with one predictable cost
Aging switches, firewalls, and wireless infrastructure make that gap even harder to close. When those technologies sit across disconnected platforms, modernization can introduce even more tools, policies, and operational complexity.
CBTS addresses this by bringing Fortinet firewalls, switching, wireless, and SD-WAN onto a single platform, with CBTS responsible for assessment, design, deployment, and 24x7 operations. The common operating model gives organizations a more consistent network and security foundation as AI increases the speed and complexity of cyber threats. Clients receive the technology and ongoing management through one subscription, giving lean IT teams a single accountable partner for network performance and security.
The model is designed around three areas of simplification:
One platform: Networking and security operate under a common architecture and policy model, reducing the gaps created by disconnected technologies.
One partner: The same Fortinet-certified CBTS engineers that design the environment support its ongoing operations, reducing handoffs between resellers, integrators, and managed service providers.
One predictable cost: Hardware, deployment, management, and ongoing refresh are combined into a predictable monthly operating cost with no upfront capital investment.
"Fortinet converges networking and security into a unified platform, and CBTS brings the engineering expertise and managed services capabilities to put that platform to work for clients," said Michael O'Brien, US RVP of Carrier Services, Fortinet. "Together, we are giving mid-market organizations a simpler way to modernize their networks, with one team supporting the environment from design and deployment through ongoing operations."
Built for mid-market, multi-site organizations
CBTS Fortinet Managed Services is designed for multi-site organizations across industries including healthcare, retail and food service, financial services, manufacturing, consumer packaged goods.
Centralized network and security management gives those organizations a more consistent way to open new locations, maintain policy across sites, and modernize infrastructure without building a larger internal engineering function. The subscription model also combines hardware refresh and ongoing management into a single predictable monthly cost rather than a series of separate technology investments.
Fortinet managed services proven at scale
CBTS has already put this model into practice for a quick-service restaurant chain with over 100 locations, replacing a mixed-vendor network with a single, fully managed Fortinet platform. The new environment brings firewall, wireless, switching, and SD-WAN under one managed service, reducing cost and complexity while creating room for future growth.
The client's environment is managed through a dedicated dashboard, providing visibility into its network while maintaining separation from other managed environments.
CBTS is a Fortinet Expert-tier partner with certified engineers who design, deploy, and manage Fortinet environments. CBTS Fortinet Managed Services is available across North America now.
Organizations do not need to be on Fortinet today to benefit. The CBTS service includes migration, with a dedicated project manager keeping the transition seamless. CBTS can also show how Fortinet integrates with their existing technology and third-party solutions.
Learn more about CBTS Fortinet Managed Services.
Register for the upcoming CBTS and Fortinet webinar.
CBTS is a leading technology services company that designs, builds, and operates resilient technology foundations for mid-market and enterprise organizations across North America. Offering expertise in AI, data, applications, platforms, and security, CBTS combines the technical depth of a large integrator with the flexibility and client focus of a specialized partner. Founded in 1994 and headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, CBTS and its OnX Canada division serve more than 3,000 clients. CBTS has been named CRN Tech Elite 250 for seven consecutive years and ranks #49 on the CRN Solution Provider 500. Learn more at cbts.com.
Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT) is a driving force in the evolution of cybersecurity and the convergence of networking and security. Our mission is to secure people, devices, and data everywhere, and today we deliver cybersecurity everywhere our customers need it with the largest integrated portfolio of over 50 enterprise-grade products. Well over half a million customers trust Fortinet's solutions, which are among the most deployed, most patented, and most validated in the industry. The Fortinet Training Institute, one of the largest and broadest training programs in the industry, is dedicated to making cybersecurity training and new career opportunities available to everyone. Collaboration with esteemed organizations from both the public and private sectors, including Computer Emergency Response Teams ("CERTS"), government entities, and academia, is a fundamental aspect of Fortinet's commitment to enhance cyber resilience globally. FortiGuard Labs, Fortinet's elite threat intelligence and research organization, develops and utilizes leading-edge machine learning and AI technologies to provide customers with timely and consistently top-rated protection and actionable threat intelligence. Learn more at https://www.fortinet.com, the Fortinet Blog, and FortiGuard Labs.

Shares of Fortinet (FTNT -0.33%) were trading sharply lower on Wednesday, falling as much as 3.4% in early trading and were still down 2.9% as of 12:27 p.m. ET.
The catalyst that sent the cybersecurity stock lower was a report that an artificial intelligence (AI) start-up is looking to make a splash in the industry.
Image source: The Motley Fool.
A new threat?
Reports emerged late yesterday that AI start-up OpenAI was in preliminary talks to acquire security research and cybersecurity company Trail of Bits, according to a story first reported by The Information. The privately held cybersecurity company made a name for itself identifying and securing vulnerabilities in open-source software.
The report suggested this might be an opening volley by OpenAI in a bid to become a cybersecurity contender.
This isn't the first time OpenAI and Trail of Bits have been linked. Several months ago, the pair launched the Patch the Planet initiative, aimed at identifying and securing exploitable vulnerabilities in open source software. During the first week alone, the initiative exposed hundreds of vulnerabilities and security issues and created fixes to secure them.

If this all seems oddly familiar, investors need only recall the collapse of many software-as-a-service (SaaS) stocks to kick off 2026. The debut of AI start-up Anthropic's Claude model raised fears that AI would ultimately replace many existing software offerings. In the ensuing months, SaaS stocks have recovered as investors have come to realize that the truth is much more nuanced and that many of these offerings aren't easily replaced.
Fortinet stock has gained 120% so far this year, with a corresponding increase in its valuation. At 54 times forward earnings and 49 times next year's expected earnings, any bit of bad news could drive the stock lower.
That said, since its IPO in late 2009, Fortinet has established itself as a force in the cybersecurity space, with its stock gaining more than 11,000%. This illustrates an important truth: Sometimes, you get what you pay for.

ICS:
Hi, what are you looking for?
A suspected state-sponsored threat actor exploited multiple Fortinet vulnerabilities in an attack against a telecommunications organization, Palo Alto Networks reports.
The intrusion, attributed to UNC5820 (tracked by Palo Alto Networks as CL-STA-0954), occurred in September 2024 and resulted in long-term access to the victim’s environment.
Initial access was obtained through the exploitation of a critical remote code execution (RCE) bug in FortiManager, tracked as CVE-2024-47575 and patched in October 2024 as a zero-day.
Shortly after the patches were rolled out, Mandiant warned that UNC5820 had been exploiting the flaw, named FortiJump, since at least June 2024.
A fresh report from Palo Alto Networks shows that UNC5820 also exploited CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal vulnerability affecting multiple Fortinet products, as part of the same intrusion.
Impacting FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager and patched in April 2026, the security defect could allow authenticated attackers to write or delete arbitrary files. Fortinet flagged its exploitation as a zero-day at the time of disclosure.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
On Friday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2025-61624 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, urging federal agencies to patch it immediately.
UNC5820 appears to have exploited the path traversal as a zero-day to deploy a previously unknown FortiGate implant dubbed PeerStitch.
The ARM64 malware resides in memory, avoids opening listening ports or initiating outbound network connections, and communicates through the traffic generated by legitimate processes on the appliance.
As part of the observed attack, UNC5820 exploited FortiJump to access a central FortiManager instance, registered a rogue Virtual FortiGate appliance, and exfiltrated a configuration archive containing details on FortiManager, more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, and the victim’s network.
UNC5820 exploited CVE-2025-61624 to gain root access to the underlying firewall operating system, dropping a script to initiate the PeerStitch deployment.
Written in C, the implant acts as a ‘one-shot process memory patching injector’ targeting the central system and traffic logging, and the IKE/IPsec VPN service daemons in FortiOS to create a covert, memory-resident communication bridge between them and bypass default FortiOS security validations.
As part of the attack, the threat actor was also seen impersonating FortiManager in FortiGate-to-FortiManager (FGFM) communications to issue commands from external infrastructure and “took extensive measures to eliminate forensic artifacts”.
According to Palo Alto Networks, UNC5820 asserted the management identity either by terminating the authentic FortiManager’s session by exploiting CVE-2024-26008, or by reusing exfiltrated secrets and authenticating as the legitimate FortiManager.
“The discovery of the PeerStitch implant demonstrates the increasing technical maturity of edge-device malware. By operating as a one-shot injector, avoiding persistent disk artifacts and building a covert inter-process communication bridge inside process memory, the attackers achieved sustained persistence while evading traditional monitoring,” Palo Alto Networks notes.

Can Fortinet's SASE Momentum Propel the Stock to New Highs?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 7:47 AM CDT 3 min read
Fortinet FTNT is gaining traction with its push to converge firewall and secure access service edge (SASE) technologies, positioning the stock for upside. At its SASE Summit 2026, highlighted on Oct. 8, the company outlined how its Unified SASE platform is evolving to secure AI applications and autonomous agents alongside human users.
Fortinet is addressing sovereignty demands through FortiSASE Outpost, which extends inspection and enforcement to on-premises and colocation sites under centralized cloud management, and FortiSASE Sovereign, a private SASE model that customers or service providers can run on their infrastructure.
This builds on the FortiGate 1200G series launched with FortiSASE Outpost in July, which combines ASIC-powered local enforcement with cloud-delivered security. The strategy is showing up in results. In second-quarter 2026, the combined SASE Firewall business, spanning Secure Networking and Unified SASE, grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings rose 35%, while FortiSASE billings more than doubled. Billings jumped 33% year over year to $2.37 billion, and revenues climbed 26% to $2.05 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Fundamentals reinforce the outlook. Product revenues surged 52% to $773 million, with management expecting attached services to boost service revenue growth in the second half. Meanwhile, the non-GAAP operating margin hit a second-quarter record of 38%.
Backed by this momentum, Fortinet raised its 2026 outlook and now expects revenues of $8.02-$8.18 billion, implying 19% growth, billings of $9.35-$9.55 billion and service revenues of $5.18-$5.22 billion. Non-GAAP operating margin is projected at 35-37%, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.41-$3.47. For the third quarter, it expects revenues of $2.01-$2.10 billion, billings of $2.25-$2.35 billion and non-GAAP EPS of 83-87 cents.
With SASE emerging as a growth engine and guidance pointing to sustained billings strength, Fortinet appears well placed to extend its momentum, paving the way for the stock to reach new highs.
How Fortinet Stacks Up Against PANW and ZS in SASE
Fortinet faces competition in SASE from Palo Alto Networks PANW and Zscaler ZS. Palo Alto Networks' Next-Generation Security ARR, which includes SASE, grew 63% to $9.10 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter 2026, while SASE competitive displacements totaled about $450 million for the fiscal year.
Palo Alto Networks expects fiscal 2027 NGS ARR of $11.08-$11.18 billion. Zscaler, a cloud-native zero-trust provider, grew ARR 25% to $3.77 billion in the same quarter and ended with more than 950 Zero Trust Everywhere enterprises. Zscaler projects fiscal 2027 ARR of $4.40-$4.43 billion. Unlike Zscaler's cloud-delivered approach, Fortinet offers on-premises, hybrid and sovereign SASE deployments.
FTNT's Share Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Fortinet shares have gained 116% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Security industry and the broader Computer and Technology sector's growth of 81.8% and 15.8%, respectively.
From a valuation standpoint, FTNT appears overvalued, trading at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings ratio of 45.52, higher than the sector's average of 19.44. The company carries a Value Score of F.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Fortinet's earnings is pegged at $3.45 per share for 2026, which implies year-over-year growth of 25%.

3 Reasons Why Growth Investors Shouldn't Overlook Fortinet (FTNT)
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 10:45 AM CDT 3 min read
Investors seek growth stocks to capitalize on above-average growth in financials that help these securities grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. However, it isn't easy to find a great growth stock.
By their very nature, these stocks carry above-average risk and volatility. Moreover, if a company's growth story is over or nearing its end, betting on it could lead to significant loss.
However, the task of finding cutting-edge growth stocks is made easy with the help of the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects.
Our proprietary system currently recommends Fortinet (FTNT) as one such stock. This company not only has a favorable Growth Score, but also carries a top Zacks Rank.
Studies have shown that stocks with the best growth features consistently outperform the market. And for stocks that have a combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy), returns are even better.
While there are numerous reasons why the stock of this network security company is a great growth pick right now, we have highlighted three of the most important factors below:
Earnings growth is arguably the most important factor, as stocks exhibiting exceptionally surging profit levels tend to attract the attention of most investors. And for growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is definitely preferable, and often an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.
While the historical EPS growth rate for Fortinet is 42.7%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 24.9% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 12.2%.
Asset utilization ratio -- also known as sales-to-total-assets (S/TA) ratio -- is often overlooked by investors, but it is an important indicator in growth investing. This metric shows how efficiently a firm is utilizing its assets to generate sales.

NET vs. FTNT: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 7:42 AM CDT 5 min read
Cloudflare NET and Fortinet Inc. FTNT are well-known players in the cybersecurity domain. While Cloudflare provides a cloud-native platform spanning network security, application security and connectivity, Fortinet combines a variety of hardware and cloud-based security solutions.
Both NET and FTNT are riding key industry trends, driven by the mounting incidents of credential theft, remote desktop protocol breaches and social engineering-based strikes by malicious actors. However, from an investment perspective, one stock offers a more favorable outlook than the other right now. Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which stock offers a more compelling investment case.
Cloudflare is seeing stronger demand for its SASE and Zero Trust offerings as companies look to adopt AI more securely. Management said the key reason big companies are approaching Cloudflare is that they know they need AI but want to deploy it securely. This is creating new opportunities for the company's SASE and Zero Trust platforms, particularly as enterprises need to secure AI agents in addition to human users.
Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach gives it an advantage in this market. Management said companies will have more AI agents working across their organizations and will need a security model designed for these agents. In one example, a large U.K. government agency was evaluating a first-generation Zero Trust provider but reconsidered the project after discussing its plans for AI agents with Cloudflare. Management said the agency canceled its existing request for proposal and is now reevaluating the project with an agents-first approach. Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach has helped its SASE and Zero Trust platforms gain significant share over the past six months.
However, Cloudflare's non-GAAP gross margin was 73.1% in the second quarter of 2026, down 320 basis points from 76.3% a year ago. The main issue is the changing mix of traffic on Cloudflare's network. As paid traffic grows relative to free traffic, a larger portion of Cloudflare's network costs is being allocated to cost of revenue. This shows that Cloudflare is handling more traffic that requires infrastructure and network resources, putting pressure on gross margins.
This is particularly relevant as AI workloads and machine-to-machine traffic expand. These workloads can drive more usage and revenues, but they also require Cloudflare to provide more compute, network and storage capacity. Although management expects gross-margin pressure to stabilize, continued growth in AI and developer workloads could require higher infrastructure spending. This could limit near-term margin expansion even as revenues continue to grow rapidly.
Fortinet is seeing strong demand for its SASE Firewall as enterprises upgrade network security to support AI workloads, cloud environments and distributed workforces. In the second quarter of 2026, Fortinet's SASE Firewall business grew 34% to more than $2 billion. Unified SASE billings increased 35%, while FortiSASE billings grew more than 100% year over year. FortiSASE adoption also reached 90% of Fortinet's large-enterprise installed base.
Fortinet believes its SASE Firewall can address a larger market than cloud-only SASE solutions. The company combines firewall, SASE and hybrid mesh capabilities on its FortiOS platform and supports both cloud and on-premises deployments. Management believes this opportunity could be two to three times larger than the cloud-only SASE market. Demand for sovereign SASE is also increasing as enterprises and service providers look for better data privacy, local processing and performance.
AI is adding another growth driver. As AI applications increase machine-to-machine and data-center traffic, customers need better visibility and control over network traffic. Fortinet said AI is accelerating the convergence of networking and security. The company is also seeing AI data center wins, including an eight-figure deal with a cloud provider offering generative AI infrastructure.
The growth in SASE could also support Fortinet's financial performance. Product revenues increased 52% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while service revenues grew 14% year over year. Service billings increased 26% year over year, and management expects service revenue growth to improve in the second half of 2026. New SASE and SD-WAN services can add to Fortinet's recurring service revenues as customers expand their deployments. With strong SASE demand, AI-driven security needs and growing adoption of sovereign SASE, the SASE Firewall could become an important driver of Fortinet's product and service revenue growth.
How do Earnings Estimates Compare for NET & FTNT?
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NET's 2026 and 2027 EPS is pinned at $1.26 and $1.72, respectively. The estimates for fiscal 2026 and 2027 have remained unchanged over the past 30 days.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FTNT's 2026 and 2027 EPS is pegged at $3.45 and $3.85, respectively. The estimates for 2026 and 2027 have both been revised up by 3 cents over the past 30 days.
NET vs. FTNT: Price Performance and Valuation
Year to date, shares of NET and FTNT have surged 76.6% and 140.2%, respectively.
NET Vs. FTNT: YTD Price Return Performance
Currently, FTNT is trading at a forward sales multiple of 15.77X, significantly lower than NET's forward sales multiple of 34.93X. FTNT's reasonable valuation makes it more attractive for investors looking for value and stability.
NET vs. FTNT: Forward 12-Month P/S Ratio
Conclusion: Buy FTNT, Sell NET Right Now
Both Cloudflare and Fortinet are key players in the cybersecurity space. However, Cloudflare's gross margins remain under pressure as higher paid traffic and AI workload usage increase infrastructure costs. In contrast, Fortinet shows steadier execution, with strong adoption of FortiSASE, Unified SASE and sovereign SASE. Further, FTNT's reasonable valuation offers some downside protection as well, making the stock an attractive buy, particularly for investors seeking exposure to cybersecurity growth at a fair price.
Currently, Fortinet carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), making the stock a stronger pick over Cloudflare, which has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

Paris, France – October 14, 2026 – Atos, a global leader of AI-powered digital transformation, today announces that it is expanding its longstanding partnership with Fortinet, a global cybersecurity leader, from a country-led to a global engagement model. The agreement will help organizations strengthen security across hybrid and multi-cloud environments worldwide through a unified framework including reselling and managed cybersecurity services. It will also align joint business development, customer engagement, service delivery and competitive commercial terms globally to address organizations' growing cybersecurity challenges.
Clients contend with escalating cyber threats and ransomware attacks, increasingly complex digital environments, expanding digital transformation programs, stricter regulatory requirements and a persistent shortage of cybersecurity skills. The strengthened Atos Fortinet partnership will combine advanced security technologies with managed security capabilities on a global scale.
Through integrated solutions and consistent services worldwide, the partnership will enable organizations to enhance protection and visibility across cloud and on-premises environments, simplify security operations, accelerate threat detection and remediation, and gain the scalability and flexibility required to pursue their digital transformation securely.
Fortinet's advanced cybersecurity technologies and engagement support across geographies and Atos' extensive expertise in managed security services, consulting and integration, as well as its global delivery capabilities and network of Security Operations Centers, will provide organizations with more innovative and scalable services to strengthen cyber resilience and support secure digital transformation, with a direct impact on operational efficiency. Over the years, Atos and Fortinet joint offering embraced customers' ongoing challenges, allowing them to benefit from Atos' cybersecurity services embedding Fortinet's latest technologies.
Günter Koinegg, global head of cybersecurity services, Atos, said: "Our expanded partnership with Fortinet aligns with our strategy to harness leading technology ecosystems to deliver integrated, outcome-driven solutions for our clients. By combining Fortinet's advanced cybersecurity technologies with Atos' consulting, integration and managed security expertise, we can provide consistent and scalable protection across hybrid and multi-cloud environments and help clients address the security challenges in the AI era."
Thomas Desrues, SVP channel sales international, Fortinet, said: "Elevating our long-standing partnership from a country-led model to a globally coordinated alliance builds on the strong complementarity between Atos' expertise in digital transformation, systems integration, and managed security, and Fortinet's leadership in cybersecurity innovation focusing on Secure Networking, Unified SASE and AI-Driven Security Operations. Through a unique combination of global scale, shared innovation, and local expertise, we provide the AI-Native Security Fabric organizations need to strengthen cyber resilience and navigate the growing demands for sovereignty, high performance, and security in AI environments."
This strengthened framework complements Atos' existing offerings spanning network security, SOC services, Zero Trust, cloud security and SASE architecture (Secure Access Service Edge), as well as cyber resilience.
Atos Group's cybersecurity services and products
As a global cybersecurity leader with more than 6,500 experts and 205 cybersecurity patents, Atos Group helps organizations navigate the evolving threat landscape with end-to-end, AI-powered security, enabling their pursuit of digital sovereignty and trust.
Cybersecurity services, delivered under the Atos brand, offer an integrated blend of strategic consulting, solution integration and continuous managed security services – spanning the entire security lifecycle. With a global network of 17 security operations centers (SOCs) processing more than 31 billion security events per day and serving over 2,000 trusted customers, Atos cybersecurity services deliver a proactive, globally informed approach to securing operations. Its teams operate with deep industry expertise across all sectors, ensuring robust data protection, regulatory compliance, and business continuity worldwide.
Cybersecurity products delivered under the Eviden brand consist of a sovereign portfolio built on three complementary areas of expertise: data encryption, identity and access management, and digital identity. Developed and manufactured in Europe, Eviden cybersecurity products comply with the highest European certification standards to safeguard sensitive data, secure digital access and protect the identities across users, systems, and connected devices.
Atos is the Atos Group brand dedicated to AI-powered, secure, end-to-end digital services. Atos designs, develops, and operates critical digital environments that drive performance, resilience and sovereignty, helping public and private organizations worldwide retain control over their data and infrastructures, while meeting regulatory requirements.
With more than 52,000 employees serving over 4,500 clients across 54 countries, Atos helps modernize core IT systems, accelerate cloud and data transformation, strengthen cybersecurity, and deliver secure digital workplace environments to support its clients, its employees and society. Atos also provides consulting and advisory services through its Atos Amplify brand.
A trusted partner in operating complex and mission-critical environments, Atos supports organizations across highly regulated and sovereign contexts.
Atos Group is a global leader in digital transformation with c. 54,000 employees and annual revenue of c. €7.2 billion, operating in 54 countries under two brands - Atos for services and Eviden for products and systems. European number one in cybersecurity and a leader in cloud, Atos Group is committed to a secure and decarbonized future and provides tailored AI-powered, end-to-end solutions for all industries. Atos Group is listed on Euronext Paris.

GovWare 2026 puts Fortinet in focus for Asia-facing growth
Fortinet (FTNT) is drawing fresh attention as it heads into GovWare 2026 in Singapore, a high profile cybersecurity conference where management plans to highlight networking and security offerings.
The event arrives after the stock hit a new 52 week high, following earnings that topped consensus expectations and contributed to a stronger momentum narrative for the cybersecurity provider.
Over the past year, Fortinet has shifted from a momentum story on paper to one investors can see in the chart. The share price has delivered a 147.74% year to date return and a 1 year total shareholder return of 129.14%, building on a three year total shareholder return of 226.24% that has kept upward pressure on the current US$192.94 level.
