Fortinet Reports Strong Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
Exceeds high end of second quarter guidance on revenue and profitability
Raises 2026 revenue guidance to 19% year over year growth
•Revenue grew 26% year over year to $2.05 billion
•Product revenue grew 52% year over year to $773 million
•Billings grew 33% year over year to $2.37 billion1
•GAAP earnings per share grew 44% year over year to $0.82
•Non-GAAP earnings per share grew 41% year over year to $0.901
SUNNYVALE, Calif. - July 29, 2026 - Fortinet® (Nasdaq: FTNT), a global cybersecurity leader driving the convergence of networking and security, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
“We are very pleased with our excellent second quarter results, which reflect the differentiated value of our innovation in the AI Era,” said Ken Xie, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Fortinet. “Our results reflect that customers value Fortinet’s unique ‘SASE Firewall’, with leading firewall, SD-WAN and SASE functionality integrated together on our single FortiOS operating system and powered by our purpose-built FortiASIC, offering customers flexible deployment in a sovereign form factor, on-prem and in the cloud.”
•Announced a strategic collaboration with Intel to develop Fortinet Security Processor 6 (SP6), combining Fortinet’s proprietary, purpose-built security processor expertise with Intel’s advanced design, development, packaging, and manufacturing capabilities to accelerate SP6 development while strengthening the resilience and diversity of Fortinet’s global supply chain.
•Launched the FortiGate 1200G series with FortiSASE Outpost, combining local enforcement and cloud-delivered security to address customers’ evolving sovereignty, performance, and AI infrastructure requirements. The convergence of firewall and SASE technologies creates a new “SASE Firewall” market built for the realities of today’s hybrid world.
•Launched FortiSOC, a new cloud-delivered SOC platform that brings together six core security operations functions into a single AI SOC experience designed to simplify and scale modern security operations.
•Expanded FortiEndpoint converging multiple endpoint security innovations into one agent to help security teams safely enable AI adoption, strengthen data security, improve risk visibility, and simplify operations.
•Partnered with Anthropic on Project Glasswing (Mythos), OpenAI on Project Daybreak (GPT 5.5 Cyber), and NVIDIA as a founding member of its recently announced Open Secure AI Alliance for AI Safety and Security.
•Moody’s Ratings upgraded Fortinet’s senior unsecured notes rating to A3 from Baa1 and its senior unsecured shelf rating to (P)A3 from (P)Baa1, the highest rating of any public cybersecurity company.
For the third quarter of 2026, Fortinet currently expects:
•Revenue in the range of $2.010 billion to $2.100 billion
•Billings in the range of $2.250 billion to $2.350 billion
•Non-GAAP gross margin in the range of 79.0% to 81.0%
•Non-GAAP operating margin in the range of 35.0% to 37.0%
•Diluted non-GAAP net income per share in the range of $0.83 to $0.87, assuming a non-GAAP effective tax rate of 18%. This assumes a diluted share count of 741 million to 745 million.
For the fiscal year 2026, Fortinet currently expects:
•Revenue in the range of $8.020 billion to $8.180 billion
•Service revenue in the range of $5.180 billion to $5.220 billion
•Billings in the range of $9.350 billion to $9.550 billion
•Non-GAAP gross margin in the range of 79.0% to 81.0%
•Non-GAAP operating margin in the range of 35.0% to 37.0%
•Diluted non-GAAP net income per share in the range of $3.41 to $3.47, assuming a non-GAAP effective tax rate of 18%. This assumes a diluted share count of 741 million to 745 million.
These statements are forward looking and actual results may differ materially. Refer to the Forward-Looking Statements section below for information on the factors that could cause our actual results to differ materially from these forward-looking statements.
Our guidance with respect to non-GAAP financial measures excludes stock-based compensation, amortization of acquired intangible assets, gain on intellectual property matters and a tax adjustment required for an effective tax rate on a non-GAAP basis, which differs from the GAAP effective tax rate. We have not reconciled our guidance with respect to non-GAAP financial measures to the corresponding GAAP measures because certain items that impact these measures are uncertain or out of our control or cannot be reasonably predicted. Accordingly, a reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to the corresponding GAAP measures is not available without unreasonable effort.
Fortinet will host a conference call today at 1:30 p.m. Pacific Time (4:30 p.m. Eastern Time) to discuss the earnings results. A live webcast of the conference call and supplemental slides will be accessible from the Investor Relations page of Fortinet’s website at https://investor.fortinet.com and a replay will be archived and accessible at https://investor.fortinet.com/events-and-presentations.
Third Quarter 2026 Conference Participation Schedule:
•Rosenblatt Technology Summit: The Age of AI
•Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference
Members of Fortinet’s management team are expected to present at these conferences and discuss the latest company strategies and initiatives. Fortinet’s conference presentations are expected to be available via webcast on the company’s website. To access the most updated information, pre-register and listen to the webcast of each event, please visit the Investor Presentation & Events page of Fortinet’s website at https://investor.fortinet.com/events-and-presentations. The schedule is subject to change.
Fortinet (Nasdaq: FTNT) is a driving force in the evolution of cybersecurity and the convergence of networking and security. Our mission is to secure people, devices and data everywhere, and today we deliver cybersecurity everywhere our customers need it with the largest integrated portfolio of over 50 enterprise-grade products. Well over half a million customers trust Fortinet’s solutions, which are among the most deployed, most patented and most validated in the industry. The Fortinet Training Institute, one of the largest and broadest training programs in the industry, is dedicated to making cybersecurity training and new career opportunities available to everyone. Collaboration with esteemed organizations from both the public and private sectors, including Computer Emergency Response Teams (“CERTs”), government entities, and academia, is a fundamental aspect of Fortinet’s commitment to enhance cyber resilience globally. FortiGuard Labs, Fortinet’s elite threat intelligence and research organization, develops and utilizes leading-edge machine learning and AI technologies to provide customers with timely and consistently top-rated protection and actionable threat intelligence. Learn more at https://www.fortinet.com, the Fortinet Blog or FortiGuard Labs.

Whether you are buying kibble for a pet or ordering takeout for dinner, you likely interact with digital giants Chewy (CHWY +4.87%) and DoorDash (DASH -0.96%). But which is the better buy?
Chewy dominates the online pet supplies market with a subscription-heavy model that ensures predictable revenue. DoorDash serves as a logistics backbone for local delivery across diverse retail categories. Both companies utilize massive logistics networks to capture consumer spending, though their paths to profitability and valuation multiples vary significantly for investors.
Chewy has established itself as a leader among retail stocks by focusing exclusively on the pet category. The company sells food, supplies, and medications primarily through its website and mobile apps, serving over 21 million active customers. Its strategy relies heavily on the Autoship subscription program, which simplifies repeat purchases for pet parents and provides the business with high revenue visibility. Recently, the company expanded into physical services through Chewy Vet Care clinics and the acquisition of Modern Animal to deepen its relationship with customers.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $12.6 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 6.2% compared to the prior year. This steady increase in sales helped the company achieve net income of close to $222.8 million. While the net margin remains relatively thin at roughly 1.8%, the move into positive territory highlights a transition from early-stage expansion to a more mature and profitable operation. This stability is vital for investors looking for consistent performance in the specialty retail industry.
As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, which means its total debt is roughly equal to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with assets it expects to convert to cash within a year, is nearly 0.9x. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated free cash flow of approximately $562.4 million, which is calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since it is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
DoorDash operates a massive local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery workers across more than 40 countries. While it began with restaurant delivery, it has expanded into grocery stores, convenience stores, and other retail categories. The company leverages its DashPass membership program, which exceeded 35 million members by the end of 2025, to drive customer loyalty and more frequent orders. In addition to delivery commissions, the company generates revenue through advertising solutions for its merchant partners, creating a diversified income stream.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $13.7 billion, showing robust growth of approximately 27.9% over the previous year. This rapid expansion was accompanied by a significant improvement in profitability, as the company reported net income of roughly $935.0 million. Its net margin reached approximately 6.8%, a substantial rise from previous years when the company was still reporting losses. The combination of high double-digit revenue growth and expanding profitability makes it a compelling option for those seeking momentum in the tech-enabled logistics space.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating that total debt is much lower than shareholder equity. Its current ratio stands at nearly 1.4x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations. The company generated impressive free cash flow of close to $1.8 billion in fiscal 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation because this non-cash expense is added back during the accounting process.
Chewy faces intense competition from e-commerce giants and large mass retailers. It specifically faces pressure from Amazon, which competes on price and delivery speed across the pet category. Operational risks include potential disruptions to its complex fulfillment network and a heavy reliance on third-party cloud infrastructure providers. Furthermore, the company must navigate strict legal and regulatory compliance requirements related to its pharmacy and veterinary services, where non-compliance could lead to significant sanctions or the loss of operating licenses.
DoorDash faces significant legal and regulatory challenges, particularly regarding the classification of its delivery drivers as independent contractors. Changes in labor laws could force the company to reclassify these workers, which would materially increase costs and complicate its operating model. The market for local delivery is also highly competitive, with Delivery Hero and other logistics platforms fighting for market share. Additionally, as the company processes vast amounts of sensitive personal data, it remains a target for cybersecurity attacks that could damage its brand reputation and lead to costly litigation.
Chewy offers a lower valuation through its P/S ratio, which measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months, while DoorDash trades at a higher Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Chewy and DoorDash both operate in the digital commerce and delivery spaces, taking products from order pages to customers' doorsteps. But as consumers battle ever-higher prices for basics like gas and groceries, can Chewy and DoorDash continue their growth trajectories? In the current economic environment, I'm looking at which company can keep customers coming back.
DoorDash is nearly 10 times the size of Chewy by market cap, and it's still growing much faster. It can use its blistering revenue growth to invest in improving its digital logistics network, which drives more orders and DashPass sign-ups. DashPass is the thing to watch here, as it can be a helpful measure of DoorDash's customer retention. In the second quarter, DashPass customers generated 75% of U.S. grocery and retail orders. DoorDash will report Q3 results on Nov. 4.
Chewy stock dropped 11% after its Q2 earnings release in September despite solid revenue growth as management pointed to continued pressure for the pet industry, evidenced by fewer treat and other discretionary sales. But it isn't all treats and toys at Chewy. While it continues to expand its pet health services, it also maintains a robust roster of Autoship customers, who comprise nearly 85% of its sales. The bulk of these sales come from consumables including food and medication, which aren't negotiable for pet owners.
Autoship sales jumped modestly year over year and net sales per active customer continued to increase in Q2. Despite its slower growth, I like Chewy as a more defensive play against a challenging consumer landscape. Plus, with the stock nearly cut in half over the past year, and valuations either lower than or in line with the broader industry average, Chewy stock may have room for a big improvement over the next year or so, provided it maintains or improves operational efficiency and keeps its loyal customers happy.

A Palm Beach County woman is suing the food-delivery giant DoorDash over allegations that a driver sexually assaulted her in the entryway of her apartment.

In the lawsuit, the attorney said DoorDash had a responsibility to make sure drivers entrusted with customers' addresses are safe and trustworthy. He argues that the company failed to investigate the driver's background adequately, including any criminal history, and failed to monitor him after letting him onto the platform.
The lawsuit also takes aim at the company's procedures for alcohol deliveries.
Mallard said that by requiring customers to interact with drivers to verify their age, DoorDash created a situation with foreseeable safety risks. What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after the major indices pulled back and tech-oriented equities fell as the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a hotter-than-expected September inflation print, pushing Treasury yields higher.
As detailed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the consumer price index rose 3.7% year-over-year in September, topping the 3.6% estimate from economists polled by Dow Jones. According to CNBC, core inflation—which excludes volatile food and energy costs—climbed 2.6% annually against expectations of 2.5%. Following the print, CNBC market data showed the 10-year Treasury yield climbed over six basis points to 5.278%, while the 30-year yield advanced past 5.59%. According to market commentators, rising yields intensify pressure on equity valuations as third-quarter corporate earnings get underway.
In remarks carried by CNBC, Franklin Templeton Institute head investment strategist Jeff Schulze noted that pressure across the long end of the curve acts as a severe valuation headwind for risk assets. Financial analysts explain that higher benchmark yields mechanically elevate the discount rate applied to corporate earnings, compressing the multiples investors are willing to pay for equities. Ultimately, CNBC noted that when sticky inflation dampens expectations for monetary easing, the repricing falls heaviest on high-multiple growth and gig-economy sectors whose projected cash flows sit furthest in the future.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

What Is DoorDash (DASH) Building With Loyalty Tools Across 80,000 Restaurants?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 12:18 PM CDT 3 min read
DoorDash (NasdaqGS:DASH) is rolling out new loyalty and marketing tools to more than 80,000 restaurants that use third-party POS systems.
The tools form part of the wider DashOS platform and are designed to help restaurants run automated rewards and targeted customer campaigns.
DoorDash is positioning DashOS as an engagement and data layer that connects restaurant ordering channels with customer recognition features.
The DashOS loyalty and marketing rollout to third-party POS partners is only one piece of the broader DoorDash story. We have also spotted 1 warning sign worth knowing about at DoorDash.
This push into restaurant software is still just one angle on the wider theme of infrastructure behind digital food ordering and delivery, where other companies are also building critical tools for operators, so it is worth looking at 92 AI infrastructure stocks.

DoorDash already runs a large commerce network that links restaurants, consumers, and delivery drivers in the US and abroad, so this push into loyalty tools effectively plugs software deeper into how those partners manage customer relationships. For a hospitality platform of this scale, more influence over how diners are recognised and rewarded can shift how much value restaurants see in staying on DashOS over time.

How could these DashOS loyalty tools matter for DoorDash's business model?
By wiring loyalty and marketing into third party POS for more than 80,000 locations, DoorDash is trying to sit closer to the transaction, not just the delivery. The firm already reports that omnichannel loyalty members order 1.8 times as often and spend about 1.75 times as much per consumer, so deeper software hooks can influence how much volume and marketing spend flows through its stack.
Does this DashOS rollout change the DoorDash Narrative investors have been using?
The Narrative leans heavily on higher margin revenue streams such as subscriptions, advertising, and merchant software, and DashOS is directly aimed at that mix. If restaurants use these tools to personalize offers and capture more loyalty sign ups, it reinforces the thesis that DoorDash can earn more from each customer without relying only on delivery fees.

What is the first concrete signal to watch to judge if this is working?
Given management already tracks loyalty behavior, the clearest early sign is any disclosed shift in the share of orders or gross profit tied to enrolled omnichannel loyalty users once the 80,000 POS integrations are in place from 2027. If that cohort's order frequency or spend mix is updated in filings or presentations, it will show how much traction DashOS is earning with restaurants and diners.

Chewy vs. DoorDash: As Consumers Tighten Their Wallets, Which Stock Can Thrive?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:40 PM CDT 7 min read
Whether you are buying kibble for a pet or ordering takeout for dinner, you likely interact with digital giants Chewy (NYSE:CHWY) and DoorDash (NASDAQ:DASH). But which is the better buy?
Chewy dominates the online pet supplies market with a subscription-heavy model that ensures predictable revenue. DoorDash serves as a logistics backbone for local delivery across diverse retail categories. Both companies utilize massive logistics networks to capture consumer spending, though their paths to profitability and valuation multiples vary significantly for investors.
Chewy has established itself as a leader among retail stocks by focusing exclusively on the pet category. The company sells food, supplies, and medications primarily through its website and mobile apps, serving over 21 million active customers. Its strategy relies heavily on the Autoship subscription program, which simplifies repeat purchases for pet parents and provides the business with high revenue visibility. Recently, the company expanded into physical services through Chewy Vet Care clinics and the acquisition of Modern Animal to deepen its relationship with customers.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $12.6 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 6.2% compared to the prior year. This steady increase in sales helped the company achieve net income of close to $222.8 million. While the net margin remains relatively thin at roughly 1.8%, the move into positive territory highlights a transition from early-stage expansion to a more mature and profitable operation. This stability is vital for investors looking for consistent performance in the specialty retail industry.
As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, which means its total debt is roughly equal to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with assets it expects to convert to cash within a year, is nearly 0.9x. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated free cash flow of approximately $562.4 million, which is calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since it is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
DoorDash operates a massive local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery workers across more than 40 countries. While it began with restaurant delivery, it has expanded into grocery stores, convenience stores, and other retail categories. The company leverages its DashPass membership program, which exceeded 35 million members by the end of 2025, to drive customer loyalty and more frequent orders. In addition to delivery commissions, the company generates revenue through advertising solutions for its merchant partners, creating a diversified income stream.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $13.7 billion, showing robust growth of approximately 27.9% over the previous year. This rapid expansion was accompanied by a significant improvement in profitability, as the company reported net income of roughly $935.0 million. Its net margin reached approximately 6.8%, a substantial rise from previous years when the company was still reporting losses. The combination of high double-digit revenue growth and expanding profitability makes it a compelling option for those seeking momentum in the tech-enabled logistics space.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating that total debt is much lower than shareholder equity. Its current ratio stands at nearly 1.4x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations. The company generated impressive free cash flow of close to $1.8 billion in fiscal 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation because this non-cash expense is added back during the accounting process.
Chewy faces intense competition from e-commerce giants and large mass retailers. It specifically faces pressure from Amazon, which competes on price and delivery speed across the pet category. Operational risks include potential disruptions to its complex fulfillment network and a heavy reliance on third-party cloud infrastructure providers. Furthermore, the company must navigate strict legal and regulatory compliance requirements related to its pharmacy and veterinary services, where non-compliance could lead to significant sanctions or the loss of operating licenses.
DoorDash faces significant legal and regulatory challenges, particularly regarding the classification of its delivery drivers as independent contractors. Changes in labor laws could force the company to reclassify these workers, which would materially increase costs and complicate its operating model. The market for local delivery is also highly competitive, with Delivery Hero and other logistics platforms fighting for market share. Additionally, as the company processes vast amounts of sensitive personal data, it remains a target for cybersecurity attacks that could damage its brand reputation and lead to costly litigation.
Chewy offers a lower valuation through its P/S ratio, which measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months, while DoorDash trades at a higher Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates.
Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Chewy and DoorDash both operate in the digital commerce and delivery spaces, taking products from order pages to customers' doorsteps. But as consumers battle ever-higher prices for basics like gas and groceries, can Chewy and DoorDash continue their growth trajectories? In the current economic environment, I'm looking at which company can keep customers coming back.
DoorDash is nearly 10 times the size of Chewy by market cap, and it's still growing much faster. It can use its blistering revenue growth to invest in improving its digital logistics network, which drives more orders and DashPass sign-ups. DashPass is the thing to watch here, as it can be a helpful measure of DoorDash's customer retention. In the second quarter, DashPass customers generated 75% of U.S. grocery and retail orders. DoorDash will report Q3 results on Nov. 4.
Chewy stock dropped 11% after its Q2 earnings release in September despite solid revenue growth as management pointed to continued pressure for the pet industry, evidenced by fewer treat and other discretionary sales. But it isn't all treats and toys at Chewy. While it continues to expand its pet health services, it also maintains a robust roster of Autoship customers, who comprise nearly 85% of its sales. The bulk of these sales come from consumables including food and medication, which aren't negotiable for pet owners.
Autoship sales jumped modestly year over year and net sales per active customer continued to increase in Q2. Despite its slower growth, I like Chewy as a more defensive play against a challenging consumer landscape. Plus, with the stock nearly cut in half over the past year, and valuations either lower than or in line with the broader industry average, Chewy stock may have room for a big improvement over the next year or so, provided it maintains or improves operational efficiency and keeps its loyal customers happy.

DoorDash Debuts Returns Program Amid New Retail Partnerships
DoorDash launched a returns program along with an expansion of its retail marketplace, according to a Wednesday (Sept. 30) press release.
The expansion involves partnerships in the apparel, beauty and home spaces, with Macy’s, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland now available options to customers, the release said.
“This is what we mean by the mall in your pocket: the brands you already know and trust, on the shelf near you, delivered as easily as walking into the mall used to be,” DoorDash Chief Revenue Officer Shanna Prevé said in the release. “You can get Macy’s or Anthropologie in as little as an hour and return it just as easily if it’s not right, no box, no label, back on the shelf and the money back in your pocket. For retailers, it means turning the stores they already have into a growth channel, not a warehouse three states away.”

The returns are possible via Dasher Returns, which lets consumers pay a flat $7.99 fee to schedule a return for an eligible retail order, and a Dasher can retrieve it from their door in as quickly as 30 minutes and bring it back to the store, according to the release. Pricing and times are subject to change.
“The return is processed on the spot, the item can go directly back on the shelf, and the consumer receives their refund within days,” the release said.
DoorDash also announced several other products and services Wednesday as it held its Dash Forward 2026 event.
These include the ability to place orders with DoorDash by sending a text rather than using an app or browser; the ability to connect DoorDash to compatible internal AI tools so employees can order team lunches or items for office restocking; a platform called DoorDash OS that connects all the DoorDash tools that are used by restaurants; a new AI assistant called DashBuddy that answers questions for Dashers; and a planned upcoming drone delivery system that will serve local businesses, the company said in several press releases issued Wednesday.
DoorDash last week announced a drone delivery partnership with Lowe’s and Google’s Wing, PYMNTS reported Thursday (Sept. 24).
The move and others like it are giving retailers a way to find out what delivery speed is worth, PYMNTS reported Friday (Sept. 25). More than 20% of orders on the DoorDash platform last year traveled between three and five miles, but those orders took almost 25% longer than shorter deliveries, mainly because pairing them with a driver took longer. Drone-delivered orders arrived in an average of 25 minutes during 2025, while some locations taking part in partner drone pilots saw order volumes grow by around 30%.
“Whether the arithmetic works will depend heavily on cost,” the report said, citing Barclays research showing autonomous delivery costs below that of conventional delivery. “Cutting several dollars from fulfillment does more to improve the economics of delivering a $15 order than a $150 order.”

Whether you are buying kibble for a pet or ordering takeout for dinner, you likely interact with digital giants Chewy (CHWY +4.87%) and DoorDash (DASH -0.96%). But which is the better buy?
Chewy dominates the online pet supplies market with a subscription-heavy model that ensures predictable revenue. DoorDash serves as a logistics backbone for local delivery across diverse retail categories. Both companies utilize massive logistics networks to capture consumer spending, though their paths to profitability and valuation multiples vary significantly for investors.
Chewy has established itself as a leader among retail stocks by focusing exclusively on the pet category. The company sells food, supplies, and medications primarily through its website and mobile apps, serving over 21 million active customers. Its strategy relies heavily on the Autoship subscription program, which simplifies repeat purchases for pet parents and provides the business with high revenue visibility. Recently, the company expanded into physical services through Chewy Vet Care clinics and the acquisition of Modern Animal to deepen its relationship with customers.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $12.6 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 6.2% compared to the prior year. This steady increase in sales helped the company achieve net income of close to $222.8 million. While the net margin remains relatively thin at roughly 1.8%, the move into positive territory highlights a transition from early-stage expansion to a more mature and profitable operation. This stability is vital for investors looking for consistent performance in the specialty retail industry.
As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, which means its total debt is roughly equal to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with assets it expects to convert to cash within a year, is nearly 0.9x. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated free cash flow of approximately $562.4 million, which is calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since it is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
DoorDash operates a massive local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery workers across more than 40 countries. While it began with restaurant delivery, it has expanded into grocery stores, convenience stores, and other retail categories. The company leverages its DashPass membership program, which exceeded 35 million members by the end of 2025, to drive customer loyalty and more frequent orders. In addition to delivery commissions, the company generates revenue through advertising solutions for its merchant partners, creating a diversified income stream.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $13.7 billion, showing robust growth of approximately 27.9% over the previous year. This rapid expansion was accompanied by a significant improvement in profitability, as the company reported net income of roughly $935.0 million. Its net margin reached approximately 6.8%, a substantial rise from previous years when the company was still reporting losses. The combination of high double-digit revenue growth and expanding profitability makes it a compelling option for those seeking momentum in the tech-enabled logistics space.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating that total debt is much lower than shareholder equity. Its current ratio stands at nearly 1.4x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations. The company generated impressive free cash flow of close to $1.8 billion in fiscal 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation because this non-cash expense is added back during the accounting process.
Chewy faces intense competition from e-commerce giants and large mass retailers. It specifically faces pressure from Amazon, which competes on price and delivery speed across the pet category. Operational risks include potential disruptions to its complex fulfillment network and a heavy reliance on third-party cloud infrastructure providers. Furthermore, the company must navigate strict legal and regulatory compliance requirements related to its pharmacy and veterinary services, where non-compliance could lead to significant sanctions or the loss of operating licenses.
DoorDash faces significant legal and regulatory challenges, particularly regarding the classification of its delivery drivers as independent contractors. Changes in labor laws could force the company to reclassify these workers, which would materially increase costs and complicate its operating model. The market for local delivery is also highly competitive, with Delivery Hero and other logistics platforms fighting for market share. Additionally, as the company processes vast amounts of sensitive personal data, it remains a target for cybersecurity attacks that could damage its brand reputation and lead to costly litigation.
Chewy offers a lower valuation through its P/S ratio, which measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months, while DoorDash trades at a higher Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates.
Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Chewy and DoorDash both operate in the digital commerce and delivery spaces, taking products from order pages to customers' doorsteps. But as consumers battle ever-higher prices for basics like gas and groceries, can Chewy and DoorDash continue their growth trajectories? In the current economic environment, I'm looking at which company can keep customers coming back.
DoorDash is nearly 10 times the size of Chewy by market cap, and it's still growing much faster. It can use its blistering revenue growth to invest in improving its digital logistics network, which drives more orders and DashPass sign-ups. DashPass is the thing to watch here, as it can be a helpful measure of DoorDash's customer retention. In the second quarter, DashPass customers generated 75% of U.S. grocery and retail orders. DoorDash will report Q3 results on Nov. 4.
Chewy stock dropped 11% after its Q2 earnings release in September despite solid revenue growth as management pointed to continued pressure for the pet industry, evidenced by fewer treat and other discretionary sales. But it isn't all treats and toys at Chewy. While it continues to expand its pet health services, it also maintains a robust roster of Autoship customers, who comprise nearly 85% of its sales. The bulk of these sales come from consumables including food and medication, which aren't negotiable for pet owners.
Autoship sales jumped modestly year over year and net sales per active customer continued to increase in Q2. Despite its slower growth, I like Chewy as a more defensive play against a challenging consumer landscape. Plus, with the stock nearly cut in half over the past year, and valuations either lower than or in line with the broader industry average, Chewy stock may have room for a big improvement over the next year or so, provided it maintains or improves operational efficiency and keeps its loyal customers happy.

Woman sues DoorDash, says driver assaulted her after vodka delivery
The lawsuit claims DoorDash's alcohol delivery rules put customers at risk.
A Palm Beach County woman is suing DoorDash after she was allegedly sexually assaulted by a delivery driver.
The lawsuit claims the driver entered her home to verify her age for an alcohol delivery and then forced her to perform oral sex.
DoorDash, in response, said it has zero tolerance for violence and is taking the allegations seriously.
A Palm Beach County woman is suing the food-delivery giant DoorDash over allegations that a driver sexually assaulted her in the entryway of her apartment.
The woman, identified in the lawsuit only as Jane Doe, said she ordered a bottle of vodka to her house on a Saturday night in March. She said the deliveryman entered her home under the guise of verifying her age, then pushed her to her knees and forced her to perform oral sex.
"DoorDash takes these allegations seriously and has zero tolerance for violence of any kind on the platform," Jenn Rosenberg, a DoorDash spokesperson, said Tuesday.
Filed Oct. 8 in West Palm Beach, the lawsuit doesn't say whether the assault was reported to or investigated by authorities, nor whether criminal charges are pending. It also omits the name of the accused driver, though Doe's Miami-based attorney Donevan Mallard said he plans to add the name once he and his client learn it.
Until then, Mallard referred to the deliveryman as John Doe and said his actions hurt his client physically, psychologically and emotionally. Mallard said the woman was humiliated by the incident and has incurred medical and counseling expenses as a result of it.
In the lawsuit, the attorney said DoorDash had a responsibility to make sure drivers entrusted with customers' addresses are safe and trustworthy. He argues that the company failed to investigate the driver's background adequately, including any criminal history, and failed to monitor him after letting him onto the platform.
The lawsuit also takes aim at the company's procedures for alcohol deliveries.
Mallard said that by requiring customers to interact with drivers to verify their age, DoorDash created a situation with foreseeable safety risks. The attorney said the company should have instructed customers that drivers do not need to enter their homes and should have trained drivers to complete alcohol verification at the doorway or another safe location.
The lawsuit contains several claims: battery and sexual battery against the unidentified driver, and three negligence claims against DoorDash over the driver's selection, his continued supervision and the company's alcohol-delivery safety procedures.
Jane Doe is seeking more than $50,000 in damages and has requested a jury trial.
Hannah Phillips covers public safety and criminal justice at The Palm Beach Post. You can reach her at hphillips@pbpost.com.

BIG W Lands on DoorDash App: 35,000+ Everyday Essentials Delivered in as fast as 60 Minutes
Tuesday, 13 October: Over 35,000* products including family and household essentials can now be delivered directly to Aussie doorsteps in as fast as 60 minutes**, with BIG W today announcing its launch on DoorDash.
Toys, electronics, clothing, pet necessities, and more can now be ordered directly through DoorDash during BIG W store trading hours, with the majority open 8am–7pm***. Delivering great value, nearly two-thirds (65%) of BIG W products on the DoorDash app are priced under $20.
The BIG W service launches today across 156 stores, offering on-demand delivery to over 80% of Australians, with plans to expand to more stores by the end of the month. This rollout follows a 10-store pilot launched on September 30.
The move sees BIG W become the first discount department store in Australia to offer ultra-convenience for customers via on-demand delivery on DoorDash.
Launching ahead of the busiest trading period of the year, families can now get rapid access to Black Friday deals, Christmas gifts, Halloween costumes and summer gear, alongside BIG W’s viral beauty, fashion, and homewares range drops.
This rollout comes after a surge in demand since BIG W’s launch of Same-Day Delivery powered by DoorDash in May, with small appliances, nursery essentials, toys, and bed linen amongst the most popular items.
Director of BIG W X, Jo Hicks said: “We know family life is chaotic and that our customers are looking for ways to ease the pressure when time isn't on their side.”
“By partnering with DoorDash we’re helping make shopping with us even more convenient, whether that means getting an emergency activity to keep the kids busy, a set of glasses right before extra guests arrive, a last minute gift or a new outfit, customers can get what they need delivered in as fast as an hour without leaving home.”
Simon Rossi, Vice President APAC, DoorDash, said: “BIG W’s huge range makes this an exciting addition to DoorDash. From toys and clothing to beauty, homewares and small appliances, Australians can now shop more than 35,000 products through both the app and web. Whether it’s getting ready for Christmas or picking up something the family needs today, we’re making it easier to shop BIG W with delivery in as fast as 60 minutes.”
The new partnership joins BIG W’s existing convenience offers, including free Pick Up from all Stores, free Metro Delivery on all orders over $59, and free Direct to Boot available at select stores.
To celebrate the launch, BIG W is offering customers 30% off through the DoorDash app if they spend more than $70 with the code BIGWDEBUT. Terms and Conditions apply.^

**Delivery times are estimates and are not guaranteed.

^ Valid 13/10/26-20/11/26 or until maximum redemptions are met prior. Order $70+ from BIG W on DoorDash (excl. fees). Max discount $25. Limit 1 redemption per customer. Use code BIGWDEBUT. Other fees (incl. delivery and service fees) still apply.

BIG W is one of Australia’s most loved brands and has been part of families’ lives for over 60 years. Our customers can choose everything for their kids, home, themselves, for leisure and for their everyday life. Our team of over 19,000 members is located in Australia, Hong Kong and Bangladesh.

Wed, October 14, 2026 at 3:12 PM CDT 3 min read
What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after the major indices pulled back and tech-oriented equities fell as the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a hotter-than-expected September inflation print, pushing Treasury yields higher.
As detailed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the consumer price index rose 3.7% year-over-year in September, topping the 3.6% estimate from economists polled by Dow Jones. According to CNBC, core inflation—which excludes volatile food and energy costs—climbed 2.6% annually against expectations of 2.5%. Following the print, CNBC market data showed the 10-year Treasury yield climbed over six basis points to 5.278%, while the 30-year yield advanced past 5.59%. According to market commentators, rising yields intensify pressure on equity valuations as third-quarter corporate earnings get underway.
In remarks carried by CNBC, Franklin Templeton Institute head investment strategist Jeff Schulze noted that pressure across the long end of the curve acts as a severe valuation headwind for risk assets. Financial analysts explain that higher benchmark yields mechanically elevate the discount rate applied to corporate earnings, compressing the multiples investors are willing to pay for equities. Ultimately, CNBC noted that when sticky inflation dampens expectations for monetary easing, the repricing falls heaviest on high-multiple growth and gig-economy sectors whose projected cash flows sit furthest in the future.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

What Is DoorDash (DASH) Building With Loyalty Tools Across 80,000 Restaurants?

DoorDash (NasdaqGS:DASH) is rolling out new loyalty and marketing tools to more than 80,000 restaurants that use third-party POS systems.
The tools form part of the wider DashOS platform and are designed to help restaurants run automated rewards and targeted customer campaigns.
DoorDash is positioning DashOS as an engagement and data layer that connects restaurant ordering channels with customer recognition features.
The DashOS loyalty and marketing rollout to third-party POS partners is only one piece of the broader DoorDash story. We have also spotted 1 warning sign worth knowing about at DoorDash.
This push into restaurant software is still just one angle on the wider theme of infrastructure behind digital food ordering and delivery, where other companies are also building critical tools for operators, so it is worth looking at 92 AI infrastructure stocks.
NasdaqGS:DASH Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026
DoorDash already runs a large commerce network that links restaurants, consumers, and delivery drivers in the US and abroad, so this push into loyalty tools effectively plugs software deeper into how those partners manage customer relationships. For a hospitality platform of this scale, more influence over how diners are recognised and rewarded can shift how much value restaurants see in staying on DashOS over time.
4 things going right for DoorDash that this headline doesn't cover.
How could these DashOS loyalty tools matter for DoorDash's business model?
By wiring loyalty and marketing into third party POS for more than 80,000 locations, DoorDash is trying to sit closer to the transaction, not just the delivery. The firm already reports that omnichannel loyalty members order 1.8 times as often and spend about 1.75 times as much per consumer, so deeper software hooks can influence how much volume and marketing spend flows through its stack.
Does this DashOS rollout change the DoorDash Narrative investors have been using?
The Narrative leans heavily on higher margin revenue streams such as subscriptions, advertising, and merchant software, and DashOS is directly aimed at that mix. If restaurants use these tools to personalize offers and capture more loyalty sign ups, it reinforces the thesis that DoorDash can earn more from each customer without relying only on delivery fees.

What is the first concrete signal to watch to judge if this is working?
Given management already tracks loyalty behavior, the clearest early sign is any disclosed shift in the share of orders or gross profit tied to enrolled omnichannel loyalty users once the 80,000 POS integrations are in place from 2027. If that cohort's order frequency or spend mix is updated in filings or presentations, it will show how much traction DashOS is earning with restaurants and diners.

New Yorkers have approximately a million opinions about NYC pizza. And DoorDash's latest list just gave all five boroughs something to complain about.
The delivery platform recently released its 2026 Top Pizza Spots, recognizing 40 local favorites nationwide for National Pizza Month, but just two New York pizzerias made the cut: Gino's NY Pizza in Buffalo and The Pizzeria in Bayport, Long Island. New York City, meanwhile, received precisely zero slots.

Before we convene an emergency pizza summit, consider the methodology. This customer-ratings list is drawn from DoorDash data and covers September 2025 through September 2026. Eligible restaurants and brands had fewer than 10 locations and at least 1,000 reviews and were selected based on the highest average overall customer ratings. (The results are grouped by region, rather than numbered from best to worst.)
So, who's representing the Empire State?
Photograph: Courtesy Gino's NY PizzaGino's NY Pizza in Buffalo, NY
In Buffalo, Gino's NY Pizza serves New York-style pies alongside specialties that put chicken and bleu cheese front and center. Its Famous Deep Bleu Chicken Pizza combines a deep-dish format with bleu cheese and marinated Buffalo chicken. Fimi's Stinger Pizza goes further, piling steak and chicken fingers onto a bleu cheese base, with a choice of hot, medium or mild. Traditionalists can stick with cheese or pepperoni slices.
On Long Island, The Pizzeria's Bayport location on Montauk Highway offers round and square pies, from a classic Grandma to considerably more loaded options. The Uncle Benny features fresh mozzarella, cup-and-char pepperoni, crumbled sausage, Mike's Hot Honey and basil. The Tri-Fecta brings together vodka sauce, pizza sauce and pesto, while the square White pie combines ricotta, mascarpone, mozzarella and white truffle oil.
"What I love about pizza is how local it is," said Ruth Isenstadt, DoorDash's head of U.S. restaurants, in the company's announcement. The company also shared ordering data that offers New York City a small consolation prize: New York-style was its fastest-growing major pizza style in 2025, with orders increasing more than 80% over 2024.
Pepperoni remained the most-ordered topping, followed by onion and sausage. White pizza led the platform's style categories with more than 3 million orders, while pineapple was ordered more often than olives, bacon, chicken or ham.
Apparently, America loves New York-style pizza. It just found its DoorDash favorites outside the city this time.

Chewy vs. DoorDash: As Consumers Tighten Their Wallets, Which Stock Can Thrive?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:40 PM CDT 7 min read
Whether you are buying kibble for a pet or ordering takeout for dinner, you likely interact with digital giants Chewy (NYSE:CHWY) and DoorDash (NASDAQ:DASH). But which is the better buy?
Chewy dominates the online pet supplies market with a subscription-heavy model that ensures predictable revenue. DoorDash serves as a logistics backbone for local delivery across diverse retail categories. Both companies utilize massive logistics networks to capture consumer spending, though their paths to profitability and valuation multiples vary significantly for investors.
Chewy has established itself as a leader among retail stocks by focusing exclusively on the pet category. The company sells food, supplies, and medications primarily through its website and mobile apps, serving over 21 million active customers. Its strategy relies heavily on the Autoship subscription program, which simplifies repeat purchases for pet parents and provides the business with high revenue visibility. Recently, the company expanded into physical services through Chewy Vet Care clinics and the acquisition of Modern Animal to deepen its relationship with customers.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $12.6 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 6.2% compared to the prior year. This steady increase in sales helped the company achieve net income of close to $222.8 million. While the net margin remains relatively thin at roughly 1.8%, the move into positive territory highlights a transition from early-stage expansion to a more mature and profitable operation. This stability is vital for investors looking for consistent performance in the specialty retail industry.
As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, which means its total debt is roughly equal to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with assets it expects to convert to cash within a year, is nearly 0.9x. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated free cash flow of approximately $562.4 million, which is calculated as cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since it is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
DoorDash operates a massive local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery workers across more than 40 countries. While it began with restaurant delivery, it has expanded into grocery stores, convenience stores, and other retail categories. The company leverages its DashPass membership program, which exceeded 35 million members by the end of 2025, to drive customer loyalty and more frequent orders. In addition to delivery commissions, the company generates revenue through advertising solutions for its merchant partners, creating a diversified income stream.
In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $13.7 billion, showing robust growth of approximately 27.9% over the previous year. This rapid expansion was accompanied by a significant improvement in profitability, as the company reported net income of roughly $935.0 million. Its net margin reached approximately 6.8%, a substantial rise from previous years when the company was still reporting losses. The combination of high double-digit revenue growth and expanding profitability makes it a compelling option for those seeking momentum in the tech-enabled logistics space.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating that total debt is much lower than shareholder equity. Its current ratio stands at nearly 1.4x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations. The company generated impressive free cash flow of close to $1.8 billion in fiscal 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation because this non-cash expense is added back during the accounting process.
Chewy faces intense competition from e-commerce giants and large mass retailers. It specifically faces pressure from Amazon, which competes on price and delivery speed across the pet category. Operational risks include potential disruptions to its complex fulfillment network and a heavy reliance on third-party cloud infrastructure providers. Furthermore, the company must navigate strict legal and regulatory compliance requirements related to its pharmacy and veterinary services, where non-compliance could lead to significant sanctions or the loss of operating licenses.
DoorDash faces significant legal and regulatory challenges, particularly regarding the classification of its delivery drivers as independent contractors. Changes in labor laws could force the company to reclassify these workers, which would materially increase costs and complicate its operating model. The market for local delivery is also highly competitive, with Delivery Hero and other logistics platforms fighting for market share. Additionally, as the company processes vast amounts of sensitive personal data, it remains a target for cybersecurity attacks that could damage its brand reputation and lead to costly litigation.
Chewy offers a lower valuation through its P/S ratio, which measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months, while DoorDash trades at a higher Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates.
Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Chewy and DoorDash both operate in the digital commerce and delivery spaces, taking products from order pages to customers' doorsteps. But as consumers battle ever-higher prices for basics like gas and groceries, can Chewy and DoorDash continue their growth trajectories? In the current economic environment, I'm looking at which company can keep customers coming back.
DoorDash is nearly 10 times the size of Chewy by market cap, and it's still growing much faster. It can use its blistering revenue growth to invest in improving its digital logistics network, which drives more orders and DashPass sign-ups. DashPass is the thing to watch here, as it can be a helpful measure of DoorDash's customer retention. In the second quarter, DashPass customers generated 75% of U.S. grocery and retail orders. DoorDash will report Q3 results on Nov. 4.
Chewy stock dropped 11% after its Q2 earnings release in September despite solid revenue growth as management pointed to continued pressure for the pet industry, evidenced by fewer treat and other discretionary sales. But it isn't all treats and toys at Chewy. While it continues to expand its pet health services, it also maintains a robust roster of Autoship customers, who comprise nearly 85% of its sales. The bulk of these sales come from consumables including food and medication, which aren't negotiable for pet owners.
Autoship sales jumped modestly year over year and net sales per active customer continued to increase in Q2. Despite its slower growth, I like Chewy as a more defensive play against a challenging consumer landscape. Plus, with the stock nearly cut in half over the past year, and valuations either lower than or in line with the broader industry average, Chewy stock may have room for a big improvement over the next year or so, provided it maintains or improves operational efficiency and keeps its loyal customers happy.

DoorDash (DASH) Stock May Look Rich After Its DashOS And AI Push

Mallard said that by requiring customers to interact with drivers to verify their age, DoorDash created a situation with foreseeable safety risks. T-Mobile Stock's 54% Drop In 2011, Much Of It In One Day
T-Mobile stock recorded its steepest fall in a market shock since 2007 during the US debt ceiling crisis. From July to October 2011, the shares fell 54%, compared with an 18% decline for the S&P 500 over the same months. Market pressure alone does not fully explain the drop. Historically, T-Mobile stock has traded through 15 market shocks since 2007. A typical event has been much milder. The stock fell 18.0% on average across these shocks, compared with 15.8% for the index. On average, the shares have dropped slightly more than the broader market.
How Long Did T-Mobile Stock Take To Recover?
The median recovery time from a low was 3.7 months, though four rebounds took more than a year. T-Mobile ultimately returned to its pre-shock high after 13 of the 14 shocks in which it fell. The stock needed 20.6 months to recover from the 2011 decline, a window that includes the one-day break in price. Following the credit crunch of summer 2007, a full recovery required 111.2 months.

Verizon has now played its hand in supporting Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature in iOS 27, which lets you easily switch between two iPhones using a single phone number. Just by unlocking the phone you want to use, your calls, texts, voicemails and Find My location automatically move over.
At launch, the feature is supported only by T-Mobile and Verizon in the US. Along with the rollout of the iPhone Duo, Verizon announced that it will charge $10 a month for the service, which will be supported “soon.” T-Mobile is charging $5 a month. AT&T is sitting this feature out for now.

T-Mobile (TMUS): Can Fiber Grow Without Consuming Too Much Shareholder Cash?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 11:53 AM CDT 4 min read
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) wants fiber to deepen relationships with wireless households while partners help finance and operate the networks. Across telecom services stocks, bundling mobile and home internet creates another recurring bill per customer. That strengthens the investment case when retention and service margins repay expansion costs.
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) trades at 12x forward P/E versus 17x trailing P/E. Trailing P/E uses the past 12 months of earnings; forward P/E uses forecast earnings. Service growth, efficiencies, and repurchases support the earnings outlook, while merger and restructuring costs weigh on reported profits. Second-quarter 2026 diluted EPS rose 5%, from $2.84 to $2.99, while net income increased approximately 1%. A lower diluted share count, helped by repurchases, allowed EPS to grow faster than total profit. The valuation looks fair if the company keeps turning network capacity into recurring cash.
Analyst consensus projects calendar 2027 adjusted EPS growth of 16.5% for T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS), versus 9.9% for AT&T Inc. (NYSE:T). These are non-GAAP estimates. The latter is a close operating peer with mobile and fiber services, but its larger directly owned fiber network and declining legacy businesses create different investment requirements. Faster earnings growth strengthens the valuation case when it produces more cash after expansion costs.

Owning the Customer While Sharing the Network
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) owns the retail customer relationships and handles marketing, sales, and support. The ventures select markets, build networks, and install connections. Its wireless customer base offers a ready audience, potentially lowering acquisition costs. Still, turning customer reach into profitable relationships requires customers to subscribe and stay. Selling another service through an existing retail operation could spread sales and support expenses over more revenue, provided discounts do not absorb those savings.
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) offers simple fiber pricing without annual service contracts. That makes retention essential: customer cash margins after wholesale charges must recover marketing, installation, and promotional spending. Industry competition for combined mobile and broadband accounts could encourage discounts that increase connections while reducing cash earned per household.
Higher take-up in neighborhoods already served can spread construction costs across more paying connections. Slow adoption leaves venture capital tied up while retail revenue builds gradually. Shared ownership reduces direct construction exposure, but the company's equity still bears the consequences of weak network utilization.
The Full Cost Extends Beyond Reported Capital Spending
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) invested $932 million and $4.6 billion in its two 2025 fiber transactions, acquiring 50% venture stakes and retail customer businesses. Announced additional transactions call for $2.7 billion at closing, with expected closings spanning 2026–2027, subject to approvals. Another $500 million is planned for an existing venture in 2027–2028. Shared ownership spreads the funding burden but leaves a substantial commitment.
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) guides to $18.4–$18.8 billion of 2026 company-defined non-GAAP adjusted free cash flow: operating cash flow less cash property and equipment purchases, including capitalized interest. Venture equity funding falls outside that deduction. Wholesale access payments already reduce operating cash flow, so subtracting them again would understate available cash.
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) generated $9.4 billion of that measure in the first half, against approximately $9.3 billion of cash buybacks and dividends. Funding those ventures requires retained cash, smaller capital returns or additional borrowing. Reducing repurchases would remove part of the support for EPS growth, connecting capital allocation directly to the forward valuation. Borrowing instead would raise interest costs before new customers generate sufficient cash. Venture losses already weigh on reported earnings. Future distributions also depend on construction needs and debt service, which can leave cash retained inside a joint venture.
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) is fairly valued at 12x forward earnings if wireless cash generation supports expansion and fiber customers deliver lasting returns after access charges and venture investment. Rising connections alone will not justify the commitment. Improving cash earned per customer and controlled follow-on funding must preserve room for shareholder returns.

A Sharp Selloff Changed the Price, Not Yet the Cash Flow
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) fell 13.2% on October 9 after SpaceX announced an approximately $8 billion agreement to acquire nationwide 800 MHz spectrum licenses. The selloff raises a valuation question: how much should investors discount a carrier generating substantial recurring cash flow for competition that could take years to materialize?
The low-band spectrum strengthens Starlink Mobile's ambitions, but regulatory approval and significant infrastructure investment remain obstacles. JPMorgan consequently saw limited immediate competitive risk, despite acknowledging SpaceX's longer-term potential.
T-Mobile ranks fifth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit. Which of the four companies attracted greater hedge fund interest, and how does T-Mobile's cash generation compare?
A Cash Generator Facing Two Competitive Tests
T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) was delivering stronger operating results before the announcement. In Q2 2026, postpaid service revenue increased 13%, total service revenue grew 9%, and core adjusted EBITDA rose 12%. Average revenue per postpaid account climbed 2% to $152.91, supporting profitability despite an increasingly competitive wireless market.
Management also raised its 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance to $18.4 billion–$18.8 billion from $18.1 billion–$18.7 billion, citing tax efficiencies and working capital improvements.
More immediate pressure comes from existing competitors. T-Mobile expects approximately 250,000 net postpaid account additions in Q3, below the roughly 304,000 anticipated by analysts, according to Reuters. Although premium-plan migrations could lift revenue per account, higher prices may also increase churn as AT&T and Verizon compete for subscribers.
Operational efficiency could help offset those pressures. Our examination of T-Mobile's AutoPilot and Dynamic CX initiatives explores whether AI-powered network management can improve margins without proportionately higher spending.
Can Earnings Growth Justify the Valuation?
At the $18.6 billion midpoint of its adjusted free cash flow guidance, T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) has considerable financial flexibility to invest in its network and return capital to shareholders. The valuation question is whether that cash generation remains resilient as competition intensifies.
According to Seeking Alpha, T-Mobile trades at 16.54 times trailing GAAP earnings and 14.40 times forward GAAP earnings, compared with sector medians of 16.26 and 14.51 times, respectively. Its forward non-GAAP P/E of 12.74 times is similarly close to the sector median of 12.52 times but substantially below its five-year average of 28.50 times. While that historical discount suggests multiple compression, it does not necessarily indicate undervaluation without sustainable earnings growth.
Consensus estimates compiled by Seeking Alpha project EPS growth of 12.71% in 2026, accelerating to 27.00% in 2027, followed by 24.86% in 2028 and 23.61% in 2029. The implied P/E declines to 11.34 times 2027 earnings and 7.35 times 2029 earnings. Those projections could make the shares appear inexpensive, provided operating leverage and subscriber profitability remain intact.
The risk is that higher retention spending, weaker customer additions, or slower revenue growth per account could undermine those expectations. SpaceX adds longer-term uncertainty, although T-Mobile's established infrastructure and subscriber base present significant barriers to entry.
SpaceX faces its own financial hurdles in challenging established carriers. Beyond acquiring spectrum, developing a competitive wireless network could require substantial additional investment. Whether those ambitions can generate returns commensurate with SpaceX's $2.2 trillion valuation remains uncertain. Our analysis of SpaceX's valuation and its challenge to telecom giants examines the financial implications of that expansion.
Analysts remain divided. Bernstein lowered its price target to $180 from $220 on October 13 while maintaining Market Perform, citing satellite competition and pricing pressure. Raymond James upgraded the stock to Outperform with a $170 target on October 12, arguing that substantial disruption could remain years away. Scotiabank maintained Outperform but reduced its target to $212 from $217.
Subscriber Economics Will Determine the Outcome
Insider Monkey tracked 85 hedge funds holding T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) in Q2 2026, unchanged from Q1. Short interest declined to 14.32 million shares as of September 30 from 17.09 million in August, representing 3.00% of the float. Both snapshots predate the SpaceX announcement and offer limited insight into subsequent positioning.
Near-term valuation will depend on subscriber additions, churn, revenue per account, and free cash flow. SpaceX's competitive significance, meanwhile, depends on its ability to translate spectrum ownership into commercially viable wireless services.
Ultimately, the October selloff repriced a potential competitive threat before measurable financial damage emerged. Whether that discount proves justified will depend on T-Mobile's ability to sustain earnings and cash generation as the wireless market evolves.

How Much Could You Lose In T-Mobile Stock?
T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock fell 16.7% over the past month, diverging from a 2.0% gain for the S&P 500. News reports tied a sharp drop on October 9 to a SpaceX spectrum deal, and AT&T, Verizon and Comcast each lost more than 12% over the same month. You may still think of a wireless carrier as a stock that holds up in a selloff. So how far has T-Mobile stock fallen in past market selloffs?
T-Mobile Stock's 54% Drop In 2011, Much Of It In One Day
T-Mobile stock recorded its steepest fall in a market shock since 2007 during the US debt ceiling crisis. From July to October 2011, the shares fell 54%, compared with an 18% decline for the S&P 500 over the same months. Market pressure alone does not fully explain the drop. The shares fell from $20.38 to $12.92 on August 2, 2011, a 37% drop in one day.
The 2008-2009 financial crisis marked the next steepest drop. T-Mobile stock fell 47% during that time, a milder decline than the 53% loss for the S&P 500. Over a longer stretch, from a peak in 2007 to a low in 2010, the stock fell 86%.
Historically, T-Mobile stock has traded through 15 market shocks since 2007. A typical event has been much milder. The stock fell 18.0% on average across these shocks, compared with 15.8% for the index. On average, the shares have dropped slightly more than the broader market.
How Long Did T-Mobile Stock Take To Recover?
The median recovery time from a low was 3.7 months, though four rebounds took more than a year. T-Mobile ultimately returned to its pre-shock high after 13 of the 14 shocks in which it fell. The stock needed 20.6 months to recover from the 2011 decline, a window that includes the one-day break in price. Following the credit crunch of summer 2007, a full recovery required 111.2 months.
Only one recovery remains unfinished. T-Mobile stock is still 43% below the high it reached before the 2025 tariff shock.
Which Of T-Mobile's Numbers Are Getting Worse?
Several underlying metrics are weakening. T-Mobile reported a slipping profit margin, slower sales growth in the latest quarter, and elevated debt compared with the broader market. The company retained 20% of its sales as operating profit over the past twelve months, down from 23% a year earlier. Sales grew 7.9% in the latest quarter from a year before, a deceleration from the 10.6% growth in the prior quarter. T-Mobile currently carries debt equal to 72.6% of its market value, against 21% for the S&P 500.
Looking toward the third quarter, whose results are still pending, management forecast fewer net new accounts and slower profit growth. During the July 23, 2026 call, the company projected about 250,000 net new postpaid accounts, down from a net 277,000 in the second quarter. Management also forecast an 8% year-over-year increase in core adjusted EBITDA, a profit measure the company guides to. This marks a step down from the 12% growth reported during that call. Management said the slowdown reflects the timing of last year's acquisitions.
Management also said changes to older rate plans in the third quarter would temporarily raise the number of accounts that leave. The company noted that smartphones are getting more expensive and that it does not intend to raise its subsidies, so customers will pay more.
When the company reports on October 28, 2026, the key metric to watch will be the net number of postpaid accounts T-Mobile added in the third quarter.
How To Act On TMUS?
Now you know TMUS better. And that's our purpose: to make you informed before you invest your money. However, making a bet on a single stock carries its own risks.

Before the SpaceX announcement, Comcast struggled with broadband subscriber losses, aggressive competition, and weaker-than-expected cash flow.

Analysts project potential losses of more than 550,000 broadband subscribers through 2026. Meanwhile, competitors have slashed prices on high-speed internet plans, forcing Comcast to lower its own rates.
Business softness and attendance slumps at Universal Studios theme parks have also dragged down its cash flows.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around CMCSA stock slipped from ‘bullish’ to ‘neutral’ over 24 hours. The stock has lost 25% year-to-date.

JOBY stock fell to a fresh annual low of $5.23 on Friday, notching two weeks in the red amid growing concerns about the company.
Last week, Barclays downgraded Joby Aviation and slashed its price target to $4 from $6, implying downside potential of about 26%.
The firm said that it had rolled out coverage of the aerospace and defense group, saying the U.S. is in the "early innings of a modern-day industrial revolution."
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Meanwhile, the company has been struggling with high cash burn and insider selling. Joby Aviation spent $202 million on cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments in the second quarter, bringing first-half 2026 cash use to $365 million, and expects to use another $385 million to $415 million in the second half of 2026.
Multiple high-ranking executives have also sold the company’s shares, with regulatory filings indicating that President of Operations Bonny Simi, CEO JoeBen Bevirt, and several other executives sold shares in recent weeks, largely to meet tax obligations.

iPhone Handoff is an iOS 27 feature that lets you share one number between two phones easily. Jeff Carlson/CNET
Verizon has now played its hand in supporting Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature in iOS 27, which lets you easily switch between two iPhones using a single phone number. Just by unlocking the phone you want to use, your calls, texts, voicemails and Find My location automatically move over.
At launch, the feature is supported only by T-Mobile and Verizon in the US. Along with the rollout of the iPhone Duo, Verizon announced that it will charge $10 a month for the service, which will be supported “soon.” T-Mobile is charging $5 a month. AT&T is sitting this feature out for now.
iPhone Handoff is similar to what the Apple Watch has done with data for a few generations: taking off one watch and putting on another automatically switches all of your information, such as activity tracking, to the new one. For example, some people use one watch during the day — perhaps the rugged Apple Watch Ultra — and switch to a slimmer, older Apple Watch at night, allowing the first to charge for the morning.
But replicating that behavior to the iPhone requires coordination with cellular providers. Each phone’s eSIM needs to be configured for iPhone Handoff by a carrier, and service needs to switch cleanly on the network side.
Ironically, the Apple Watch gets left out of the iPhone Handoff transaction: Your watch remains paired with just one iPhone, communicating with it via Wi-Fi or cellular (if that’s an option). “If neither is available,” Apple writes, “calls, messages, notifications, certain health and fitness features, Siri AI or other app experiences relayed from your paired iPhone may not be available.”
In its press release about offering the iPhone 18 Pro, T-Mobile writes, “iPhone Handoff is available on any iPhone with iOS 27 via iPhone settings and ready to use from day one on the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iPhone Duo. T-Mobile is introducing the feature at $5/month.”
When I reached out to T-Mobile asking about the charge, a spokesperson wrote via email, “The $5/month charge reflects the added service that powers the experience on both devices.”
A Verizon representative did not have further details to share.
While iPhone Handoff appears to seamlessly switch your eSIM just by picking up the phone you want to use, it’s not yet clear what else is different with this process versus just transferring your eSIM manually using your iPhone’s settings menu.
Notably absent from Apple’s news was the other major US carrier, AT&T. I contacted a spokesperson there to learn more about the company’s plans for the feature, but it sounds like it’s not a priority.
“While we see that there could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” the spokesperson replied, “our focus remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” They then pointed to “existing eSIM activation and transfer options across compatible devices.”
In addition to T-Mobile and Verizon, iPhone Handoff is currently supported by Deutsche Telekom in Germany. The UK carrier EE will also support the feature later this year, according to Apple.
Jeff Carlson writes about mobile technology at CNET, from cellular phone plans to devices and emerging technology.
